# WWI CEF War Diaries — Master Searchable Index
The single searchable index for the whole archive, merged daily by the digest task (`wwi-war-diary-daily-digest`) from the eight per-eighth indexes (`INDEX-A.md` … `INDEX-H.md`). Rebuilt from scratch each day, so corrections in the eighth indexes replace stale entries here.
- **Coverage:** 467 CEF unit war diaries with a diary line in the LAC finding aid (RG 9 III-D-3), transcribed from Library and Archives Canada digitized pages. (The ~1,587 figure in early planning counts diary volumes/folders; the guide's with-diary unit total is 467.)
- **Status (27 Oct 2026):** 13141 dated entries from 22 unit(s) so far; 13141 entries merged from 8 eighth index file(s). Date range 1914-09-15 to 1919-06-28.
- **Entries are sorted by date, then unit.** Each entry keeps: date, unit, location, people named, companies/platoons, casualties, movements, what happened — plus a pointer to the full transcript under `diaries/<unit-slug>/` (see Sources below).
- **Uncertain readings** in the transcripts are marked [uncertain]; nothing is guessed.

- **October 1917** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1917-10.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0166`–`page-0178`, `manifest.json`). October has 15 numbered pages; pp. 4–5 are absent from the LAC manifest, so 13 physical pages. No appendices listed or filed. - **November 1917** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1917-11.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0179`–`page-0191`, `manifest.json`). November has 15 numbered pages; pp. 4–5 are absent from the LAC manifest, so 13 physical pages. No appendices listed or filed. Readability note: the November hand is the same cramped hand as August–October, and many words are only partly legible — entries below record what could be read reliably. C & D Companies move south to Lebuquiere (3rd Army North) on 6 November; from then the diary covers both the 1st Army area (A & B Coys at Barlin) and the 3rd Army area (C & D Coys at Lebuquiere). The O.C. changes during the month: the diary is signed at month end by W. Stewart [uncertain], Lt. Col., not J. B. Macdonald.

- **December 1917** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1917-12.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0192`–`page-0208`, `manifest.json`). December has 19 numbered pages; pp. 4–5 are absent from the LAC manifest, so 17 physical pages. Contents page lists "Diary Text 7 Pages" but the diary text in fact runs 11 pages (pp. 6–16, 1–31 Dec); Appendices 1–3 are pp. 17–19 (congratulatory messages, 28 Nov – 24 Dec 1917). Readability note: the December hand is the same cramped hand as August–November, and many words are only partly legible — entries below record what could be read reliably. C & D Coys return from the 3rd Army area to Barlin on 6–8 Dec and begin the "Cape to Cairo" lateral light-railway line. The diary is signed at month end by J. B. L. Macdonald, Lt.-Col. Reconciliation note: the 16 Dec casualty is recorded as "Pte Cooney [uncertain] No 279834" (p. 11) but the 30 Dec entry reports "Sgt Cooney J. D. (No. 22983), awarded M.M., killed by shell fire 16th inst." — rank and number differ between the two entries and are NOT reconciled; see the transcript's reconciliation notes.

- **January 1918** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1918-01.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0209`–`page-0221`, `manifest.json`). January has 15 numbered pages; pp. 4–5 are absent from the LAC manifest, so 13 physical pages. Contents page lists "Diary Text 9 Pages" — diary text is pp. 6–14 (9 pages) and p. 15 is Appendix 1 (typed letter dated 18 Jan 1918 proposing standardisation of light-railway rules), so the contents page is exact. Readability note: the January hand is the same cramped hand as August–December, and many words are only partly legible — entries below record what could be read reliably. C Coy begins work on the Cape to Cairo lateral line; 300 Chinese labourers start on it 3 Jan; Lt-Col Macdonald is awarded the D.S.O. and Sergt Glisson the D.C.M. (10 Jan); Macdonald proceeds on leave 22 Jan and the month is signed by J. [uncertain] Stewart, Major. Reconciliation note: 1 Jan confirms Spr J. W. Cooney, No 279834, killed 16 Dec 1917, but the 30 Dec entry's "Sgt Cooney J. D., No 22983" still conflicts — not reconciled; see the transcript's reconciliation notes.

- **1915-02-07 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Unit prepared to disembark from H.M. Transport, reported to the Base Commandant at the Palais de Justice, and billeted 4 N.C.O.s and 22 men at Caserne Trupel, Rue de Lyons. | Casualties: none. | Movement: disembarked at Rouen.
- **1915-02-08 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Reported to A.D.M.S. No. II Base, indented for ordnance and stationery, arranged for the section's N.C.O.s to learn duties from the Rouen sanitary section, and sent an orderly for standing orders and daily orders. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-09 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Detailed corporals and lance corporals for duty with the Sanitary Police in the city and indented for completion of clothing. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Medically examined the entire personnel of the Sanitary Section at 8 a.m. and drew ordnance and supplies as completely as were available. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — The section's motor lorry collided with motor car 780-Y 4 at about 3 miles an hour, springing a mud guard (righted by hand, undamaged) and cracking a brass axle cap in two, the repair probably costing 4 francs. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Visited by Lieut Dickson, A.S.C., in charge of an ambulance convoy, who had orders to proceed and verbal orders for Woodhouse to accompany him; the orders were verbally confirmed at A.D.T. and orders issued for movement at 8.30 a.m. | People: Lieut Dickson. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-11 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Neufchâtel** — Unit left Rouen at 8.30 a.m. with the ambulances and arrived at Neufchâtel at 3 p.m. for the night, the Quartermaster Sergeant, groom and horse being left behind, the horse and groom attached to the Cavalry Division for transport to the destination. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Rouen → Neufchâtel.
- **1915-02-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Abbeville** — Left Neufchâtel at 6.40 a.m. and arrived at Abbeville at noon. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Neufchâtel → Abbeville.
- **1915-02-13 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arques** — Left Abbeville at 8.30 a.m., arrived at St. Omer at 3 p.m., reported to A.D.M.S., and was assigned billets at Arques, billeted at 5 p.m. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Abbeville → Arques (via St. Omer).
- **1915-02-15 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Outtersteene** — Marched out of Arques at 7.30 a.m., reported to D.M.S. Hazebrouck, the men being conveyed by ambulance to Merris and marching to billets at Outtersteene, distributed chloride of lime to units of 1st Brigade for water purification, and reported to A.D.M.S. Canadians at 8 p.m. in heavy snow (the events of 14 February are reported inside this entry). | Casualties: none. | Movement: Arques → Outtersteene (via Hazebrouck and Merris).
- **1915-02-16 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — On orders received at noon, moved the corps to new billets at Strazeele Station, occupying them by 4 p.m., and supplied 1st Brigade Office with 20 extra tins of chloride of lime and a supply to the Brigadier, 3rd Brigade. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Outtersteene → Strazeele.
- **1915-02-17 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Despatched a party by lorry to Outtersteene for house-to-house visitation to locate enteric fever among civilians, present or within six months past, and to make a sanitary survey and report, with one squad on guard during the night and a fourth squad cleaning the section's own billets. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-18 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Despatched men to complete the enteric enquiry and sanitary survey of Outtersteene and Merris. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-19 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Completed the enquiry and survey of Strazeele and personally visited houses reported by the squads in Strazeele, Merris and Outtersteene to enquire into cases of illness, none of which proved to be a reportable communicable disease, and arranged hot baths for the whole section the next morning. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-20 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Pradeele and Borre were surveyed as above. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Caestre was surveyed as above. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-22 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Caestre survey completed and Flêtre undertaken, with house-to-house enquiry into infectious diseases completed that day in Merris and Outtersteene, suspicious houses being placed out of bounds for Canadians. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-23 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Flêtre and Meteren were surveyed. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-23 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Le Havre** — Entrained with equipment from Quai Pondicherry at 4.30 P.M. | Casualties: none. | Movement: entrained at Le Havre.
- **1915-02-24 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — No separate summary is given for this date; the line appears to continue the Flêtre / Meteren survey. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-24 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Boulogne-sur-Mer** — Arrived at Boulogne-sur-Mer at 12.30 P.M., detrained; equipment stored and the company quartered at the Convalescent Camp, Boulogne. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Le Havre → Boulogne-sur-Mer.
- **1915-02-25 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Meteren survey completed and four squads placed to police Outtersteene, Merris and Strazeele in the afternoon. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-26 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Troops of 1st Brigade were re-billeted under the section's personal supervision, suspicious houses not being used, and a case of civilian enteric near Caestre was ordered cleared to Bailleul. | Casualties: civilian enteric case near Caestre cleared to Bailleul; none among the section.
- **1915-02-27 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Accompanied A.D.M.S. to visit a new area and spent the day with D.A.D.M.S. and O.C. Sanitary Section, 7th Division, preparing to take over their area, and received orders to move tomorrow. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-28 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Left Merris at 9 a.m. and marched until 8 p.m. before receiving billets. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Merris → Sailly-sur-la-Lys.
- **1915-03-01 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — Proceeded to MERRIS, destroyed horse, ordered removal and burial, paid for same, also for keep. Remark: Judging from the condition of the feet of sick horses received, it appears that there must either be a shortage of shoes, or else feet are not receiving sufficient attention. | Casualties: 1 horse destroyed. | Movement: Proceeded to Merris.
- **1915-03-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Granted temporary accommodation in the offices occupied by the O.C. Sanitary Section of the 7th Division and made rounds with him. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — Proceeded to CAESTRE, found horse dead, paid for removal, burial and keep. | Casualties: 1 horse died. | Movement: Proceeded to Caestre.
- **1915-03-02 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had the men's billets scrubbed from top to bottom, mapped out areas for inspection purposes, and instructed the section as to the nature of the work desired. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — No forage for horses or rations for men, owing to Supply Column moving to SAILLY and making no arrangements for supplies for Unit. Purchased forage out of Imprest Account. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-03 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Investigated three billets which had been occupied by an enteric case and saw to the cleansing of them. | Casualties: civilian enteric case (billets cleansed); none among the section.
- **1915-03-04 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — Removed to CROIX DU BAC. Billeted at farm between CROIX DU BAC and BAC ST. MAUR. Still without rations. Purchased forage for horses. Remark: This would be of considerable advantage in dealing with cases of skin disease, which is very prevalent here. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Removed to Croix du Bac.
- **1915-03-04 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Inspected the General's château and a factory occupied by Ordnance. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-05 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 5 sick horses from 6th. Division Mobile Veterinary Section, belonging to Canadian Division, also 2 from 2nd and 3rd Infantry Brigades. | People: 6th. Division Mobile Veterinary Section; 2nd and 3rd Infantry Brigades. | Casualties: 7 horses received.
- **1915-03-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Installed a new portable sanitary closet at the château made [uncertain] of biscuit tins, with a reversible tightly fly-proof covered seat, and had the Ordnance depot made [uncertain] and reported its defects to its O.C. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-05 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Montreal, Canada** — Mobilised under G.O. Headquarters, 4th Div., Canada, at McGill University Buildings. | Movement: mobilisation at Montreal.
- **1915-03-06 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 5 sick horses. 1 died. | Casualties: 5 horses received, 1 horse died.
- **1915-03-06 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had the factory near Ordnance cleaned by the section and made fit for billets. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-06 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Montreal, Canada** — Internal economy arranged and organised; stretcher and squad drill; instruction.
- **1915-03-07 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 1 sick horse, 1 died, 1 [uncertain] cured. | Casualties: 1 horse received, 1 horse died, 1 horse issued cured.
- **1915-03-07 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Located four infected houses and attended to them, with [uncertain] information from the local French physician. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-03-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had squads doing fatigue work or overseeing work done by others in cleaning up unsanitary billets. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-04-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Vlamertinghe** — Well pump raised, water pumped out, walls [uncertain] scrubbed and chloride of lime freely placed in it, storage still unsolved, and arranged to send an N.C.O. and four men to Poperinghe tomorrow for duty. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-04-22 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Vlamertinghe** — Squad and Sergeant Major worked in Poperinghe today and were assigned a portion of the city to inspect and correct, work reported as satisfactorily carried out. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-04-22 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Montreal, Canada** — Inspection by H.R.H. The Duke of Connaught; Khaki Convocation to graduates; Mess Dinner to His Royal Highness. | People: H.R.H. The Duke of Connaught.
- **1915-04-23 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Elverdinghe** — Remained at above mentioned farm pending further orders from Divisional Headquarters, who are moving back. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-04-24 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Elverdinghe** — Remained in same billet. Received 3 sick horses. | Casualties: 3 horses received.

- **1915-04-25 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Elverdinghe** — Received 3 sick horses. Removed in evening, leaving 1 Sergt 1 Corpl + 5 men behind for the purpose of receiving sick + wounded horses. | Casualties: 15 horses received, 24 horses evacuated.

- **1915-04-26 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Reninghelst** — Moved on to a farm about 3 Kilometres North of BOESCHEPE, but only stayed there 6 hours, removing to a farm about 3 Kilometres farther North and about 3 Kilometres South West of POPERINGHE. 4 sick horses received from advanced portion of Section. - **1915-04-26 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Vlamertinghe** — Unit arising at 2 a.m. relieved men of No. III Field Ambulance, with the lorry busy evacuating, one trip to Hazebrouck. | Casualties: wounded evacuated; none among the section.
- **1915-04-27 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Received 3 sick horses. Destroyed 1. POPERINGHE shelled in evening. | Casualties: 3 horses received, 1 horse destroyed.

- **1915-04-28 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Received 4 sick horses. Evacuated 8 to Base Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 4 horses received, 8 horses evacuated.
- **1915-04-28 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Watou** — Lorry drew supplies for the Rest Station, also clothes and blankets from Ordnance for the sick. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-04-29 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Steenvoorde** — Unit came here last night to open a place for a Rest Station for No. I Field Ambulance, chose a farm and provided accommodation for 200 sick, with [uncertain] and the lorry assisting No. I Ambulance. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Watou → Steenvoorde.
- **1915-04-30 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Received 25 sick + wounded horses. Evacuated 27 to Base Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 25 horses received, 27 horses evacuated.
- **1915-04-30 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Steenvoorde** — D.A.D.M.S. visited the Rest Station and approved, patients to be sent as soon as necessary, and half the men sent to do sanitary work at Godewaersvelde. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-04-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Wimereux** — Nothing has occurred to vary the routine of the hospital work, except the admission of some [uncertain — appears to read "mild"] cases of gas poisoning. | Casualties: gas poisoning cases admitted (number not given).

- **1915-05-04 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Proven** — Received 4 sick horses. Moved out of billet at 2 pm., Division having moved to NIEPPE. Spent night at farm near LOCRE. | Casualties: 4 horses received. | Movement: Moved to Nieppe.
- **1915-05-04 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Bailleul** — Arrived and occupied billets assigned by noon, visited by A.D.M.S. Col. Skinner. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Steenvoorde → Bailleul.
- **1915-05-04 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Wimereux / Honeault Camp [uncertain]** — Routine has assumed the character of a clearing hospital; the first cases treated with Boracic [uncertain] paste were received — 22 cases admitted and analysed (6 superficial wounds penetrating subcutaneous tissue, 8 deep penetrating wounds, 4 deep perforating wounds, 4 scalp perforating wounds) — and the diary concludes the paste's beneficial effect is limited to superficial wounds, as in deep and perforating wounds it seals up infection material and prevents drainage, and in scalp wounds it always delays healing. | Casualties: 22 cases admitted for the boracic paste trial.

- **1915-05-31 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Wimereux / Honeault Camp [uncertain]** — The work done during the past month has been similar in many details to a clearing hospital; operations consisted chiefly in the removal of foreign bodies, free incisions and drainage, and the most satisfactory subsequent treatment was a moist dressing of soda citrate and sodium chloride (Wright). | Casualties: none recorded for the day.

- **1915-06-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Vendin-lez-Béthune** — Arrived yesterday in the new area, established camp, reorganised the section, appointing a new Lance Corporal and completing four squads of four men each, addressed the men on the fly menace and breeding, improper handling of food in [uncertain] kitchens and ptomaine poisoning, instituted closer vigilance of water carts and water treatment, testing with the iodide starch reaction, divided the new area into four parts with a corporal and squad for each, and assisted A.D.M.S. to prepare a field for tent hospitals. | Casualties: none. | Movement: arrived Vendin-lez-Béthune (31 May).

- **1915-06-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Honeault Camp, France** — Patients remaining in hospital 16; patients admitted during the month: sick 238, wounded 397, total 635; the character of the cases has been of a light nature, usually requiring some minor operative work and nursing and evacuable in a short time; several interesting medical cases came under observation — pericarditis 1, Vincent's angina 1, atropine poisoning 1, typhoid 1 [uncertain] 3 paratyphoid [uncertain] — and the atropine poisoning case, following an inoculation or re-vaccination [uncertain], developed symptoms typical of atropine poisoning which subsided under treatment, returned the following day resembling meningitis, could not be confirmed by puncture, and did not react to treatment, with prominent meningeal symptoms and a strong hysterical element; the case was transferred (as written, "to No 1 Stationary Hosp.") under suspicion, and the diagnosis since received is uncertain, with no confirmation of meningitis; average days in hospital during the month 3.27. | Casualties: 635 admitted in the month (238 sick, 397 wounded); no deaths recorded.

- **1915-09-26 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Convoy arrived 9 p.m.
- **1915-09-27 | 24th Battalion | Siege Farm / Locre, Belgium** — Visited Siege Farm, where 4 stretcher bearers are with B Company; enemy shells fell near the farm most evenings, evidently aimed at nearby batteries. | People: — | Companies: B Company | Casualties: none | Locations: Siege Farm; Locre
- **1915-09-27 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Neuve Eglise** — Received 1 sick horse. | Casualties: 1 horse received.
- **1915-09-27 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Visited Aldershot camp just after it was vacated by the 29th and 31st Battalions of the 6th Brigade and found it in a very unsanitary condition, with faeces along the hedges and overflowing latrines, then planned with Capt. [uncertain] of the C.E. 3rd and Col. Colborne's 25-man fatigue to develop the Bulford spring with a trench, gravel filter and pipe to a reservoir. | People: Capt. [uncertain] (C.E. 3rd), Col. - **1915-09-28 | 24th Battalion | Wytschaete** — Took over the trenches of the right sector at 9 p.m., relieving the 25th Bn; battalion HQ at Rossignol Estaminet. | People: — | Companies: A, B, C, D | Casualties: none | Movement: Locre to the Wytschaete trenches | Locations: Wytschaete, Rossignol Estaminet, Siege Farm

- **1915-09-28 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Work began on improving the Bulford well and continued until 8 p.m., the Aldershot cleaning was finished, a sick parade for convalescents was begun with four men serious, and No. 1 Field Ambulance supplied 50 blankets after Ordnance objected to giving them. | Casualties: 4 convalescents seriously sick at sick parade; no deaths.
- **1915-09-28 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of report occurred.
- **1915-09-29 | 24th Battalion | Kemmel, Belgium** — First casualty: Pte McBride (Sanitary Squad) wounded in the left arm; shells at 7.30 p.m.; Cpl B. M. Patterson #65965 wounded through the cranium, since deceased; supplies arrived from Locre. | People: Pte McBride; Cpl B. M. Patterson #65965 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 wounded (McBride); 1 died (Patterson) | Locations: Kemmel; Locre
- **1915-09-29 | 24th Battalion | Wytschaete** — First day in the front line: snipers very active all day; enemy whizz-bangs at 1.20 p.m. with no damage; Pte Best claims a sniper at Petit Bois; working parties dispersed and returned to work. | People: Pte [uncertain] Bride, Pte Best | Companies: C | Casualties: Pte Bride (No. 12 Platoon, C Coy) wounded in the left arm by a machine-gun bullet — the battalion's first casualty | Locations: Petit Bois, S.3L
- **1915-09-29 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Neuve Eglise** — Received 2 sick horses. | Casualties: 2 horses received.
- **1915-09-29 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Work on the Bulford well practically complete, 50 "Stereophagi", 160 latrine buckets and other stores handed over from Division, a latrine put up for the women working in the [uncertain] near Neuve Eglise, and a sick parade held with four sick including one interesting case of marked photophobia. | Casualties: 4 convalescents sick at sick parade; no deaths.
- **1915-09-29 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Convoy arrived 1.30 a.m.; Nursing Sisters D. Cotton (to Anglo-Russian Hospital, Petrograd) and J. Duncan (resigned, to Wilmington, U.S.A.) departed 9.30 a.m.; convoy arrived 11 p.m. | People: D. Cotton, J. Duncan.
- **1915-09-30 | 24th Battalion | Wytschaete** — Trench, parapet and parados repairs; German periscopes broken; enemy green and red flares and a green rocket; four whizz-bangs failed to explode; dugout built in J.1, traverse in J.10 to H.3 A; two officers and 50 men working on a new trench 8 p.m.–2.30 a.m. | People: Cpl B. M. Paterson (No. 65765) | Companies: — | Casualties: Cpl Paterson dangerously wounded in the head while firing over the parapet in G.4 A about 11 p.m. | Locations: G.4 A, H.4, J.1, J.10, H.3 A
- **1915-09-30 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Neuve Eglise** — Received 3 sick horses. Issued 3 cured. | Casualties: 3 horses received, 3 horses issued cured.
- **1915-09-30 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Visited the left half of the Divisional area and found everything very satisfactory despite almost continuous rain, and held a sick parade with four sick including a practically cancerous venous angioma case [uncertain]. | Casualties: 4 convalescents sick at sick parade; no deaths.
- **1915-09-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — Improvised operating room, dispensary and officers' mess completed; fitting up of the hospital wards continues; trench drains and stone paths laid out in the hut area; lighting of the hospital inefficient — hurricane lanterns in limited numbers and sometimes only candles; general health of the unit good; routine work of the hospital being carried out satisfactorily. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-09-30 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Convoy arrived 3 a.m.; visit by Colonel John Layton Blenkinsop, Secretary to the Director General Medical Services, War Office; month-end surgical summary: 280 major operations, 6 anaerobic infections, 3 amputations (gas gangrene), post-operative mortality 5 (nearly 2%). | People: Col John Layton Blenkinsop. | Casualties: 280 major operations; 5 post-operative deaths; 3 amputations.
- **1915-10-01 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — During completion of a new trench: Pte E. [uncertain] #65984 killed; R. R. Driscoll #65285 slight flesh wound in thigh; C. W. Price #65999 perforated lung, died 2 Oct; P. Mackinnon #16066 [uncertain] slight shoulder wound, returned to duty 2 Oct. | People: Pte E. [uncertain] #65984; R. R. Driscoll #65285; C. W. Price #65999; P. Mackinnon #16066 [uncertain] | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 1 died of wounds, 2 wounded

- **1915-10-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Visited the left half of the district and found things in better order than for some time, the Bedford Camp well a success with another to be developed north of it, and started building shelters for the field kitchen; convalescents 86 remained, 11 admitted, 15 to duty, 0 to hospital, 82 remaining. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-10-01 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Hut accommodation increased by the addition of 2 huts, so the hospital can now accommodate 550 patients; still some difficulty in getting food supplies outside of rations; dysentery cases on the increase and of a more resistant nature; weather exceptionally fine, when very warm flies increase; sanitary conditions much improved. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-10-01 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Convoy arrived 5.45 a.m.
- **1915-10-02 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Enemy trench mortars; our artillery replied with 36 rounds and silenced them; an enemy sniper brought down; Pte H. Johnson #65498 slight scalp wound; W. A. Ward #66017 killed. | People: Pte H. Johnson #65498; W. A. Ward #66017 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 1 wounded
- **1915-10-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Neuve Eglise** — Received 1 sick horse. Issued 1 cured. | Casualties: 1 horse received, 1 horse issued cured.

- **1915-10-02 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of report occurred.

- **1915-10-04–05 | 24th Battalion | Locre** — First tour of duty in the trenches ended on the night of 4–5 October; relieved by the 25th Bn and returned to billets in Locre; enemy fairly active with sniping and artillery. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none reported | Movement: trenches to billets in Locre | Locations: Locre

- **1915-10-07 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Convalescents 107 remained, 5 admitted, 0 to duty, 0 to hospital, 112 remaining; visited the left half of the area and specially inspected the wash house and clothes drying place near Neuve Eglise after a complaint that clothes still had vermin after processing, finding the 1-hour soak in 2% cresol and boiling would kill all vermin if adhered to. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-10-09 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Reinforcements of seven men arrived by the hospital ship Delta on 9 October; Col Agnew, Camp Commandant, inspected the hospital; eleven hospital ships in the harbour on 10 October; troops leaving for Salonica; commenced use of water from a tank brought through pipes from the condenser on 13 October; 90% of patients in hospital from troops on Lemnos, i.e. having contracted dysentery since coming here in the majority of cases; evenings become quite cool, days very fine; amoebic dysentery becoming less, bacillary on the increase; all cases lack the very acute symptoms of early cases but are more severe owing to delay in reaching hospital. | People: Col Agnew. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-10-09 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Captains McKim and Tidmarsh returned to the unit 7 p.m.

- **1915-10-31 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Month summary (written up 31 October, covering the rest of the month): Col McKee sailed for England on the hospital ship Aquitania on 18 October and Major E. J. Williams assumed temporary command; progress of patients in hospital very slow owing to the severity of the disease, with rheumatism(?) and jaundice common sequelae to dysentery; one case of beri-beri in hospital; a tent section was opened for venereal and infectious cases — syphilis, gonorrhoea, scarlet fever, diphtheria, chicken pox, mumps and measles, 50 cases in all — with diphtheria from the Australian Rest Camp, 17 cases developing in one week; 638 cases in hospital on 18 October and an average daily state for the month of 550; the death rate in the last two weeks of September was 6 times any previous two weeks, due to cases arriving in hospital in a late stage of disease; S.S. Aquitania left for England on 21 October; high winds for 4 days blowing down some tents; General Munro, who succeeded Sir Ian Hamilton, inspected troops and hospitals on 27 October; the Welsh Division returning from the Peninsula and Australians preparing to return; many severe cases of bacillary dysentery in hospital; six post mortems held during the month; health of personnel good except among the new drafts of men, everyone seeming to develop enteritis and diarrhoea a few days after arriving on the island, the attacks as a rule not lasting longer than one week; general improvement in all supplies except equipment; besides the reinforcements of 7 men there was a further addition of 27 men and one officer, Capt. Creighton; five men of the unit were invalided home to England; all nursing sisters are comfortably accommodated in canvas huts, officers and men still in tents; buildings for ordnance stores, offices etc. not yet erected; the X ray department moved into the Operating Room building; very much cramped for room for patients, 550 being accommodated in 12 huts planned to hold 25 patients each; 18 deaths in October as compared with 4 in September, 90% being due to dysentery. | People: Col McKee; Major E. J. Williams; General Munro; Sir Ian Hamilton; Capt. Creighton. | Casualties: 18 deaths in October (90% dysentery), as compared with 4 in September; 638 cases in hospital on 18 October; average daily state 550.
- **1915-10-31 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — O.C.'s memorandum on the hospital's condition: the 25 October storm accentuated the conditions; transferring patients to the operating theatre under canvas adds considerably to shock; situation "totally unsuitable for the purpose for which it was originally intended". Surgical report (Lt-Col J. M. Elder): 1,650 patients admitted to surgical wards, 36 deaths, 450 operations, 21 deaths among operated patients; septic knee joints, anaesthesia, X-ray and laboratory work praised. Laboratory report (Capt. L. J. Rhea): clinical and bacteriological work; September examinations (urine 659, blood 179, faeces 20, sputum 25, gastric 12); typhoid group; special cases. Ambulances gifted by Mrs. Huntley Drummond, Mrs. W. R. Miller, the citizens of Montreal through Lady Allan and the citizens of Quebec through Mrs. Turner: 350 runs, 2,035 patients carried August–October, at no cost to the Government. | People: Lt-Col J. M. Elder, Capt. L. J. Rhea, Mrs. Huntley Drummond, Mrs. W. R. Miller, Lady Allan, Mrs. Turner. | Casualties: surgical wards — 36 deaths of 1,650 admitted; 21 deaths among 450 operated.

[uncertain] regulations [uncertain], and in the afternoon visited [uncertain] camp area, finding everything in good condition with wells and disinfectors slowly progressing. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-16 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Heavy snowfall (about 2 inches) overnight; tents unable to withstand the weight of snow; heating totally inadequate; still no electric light.
- **1915-11-17 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 sick horses. | Casualties: 2 horses received.

Frith's request planned a "fire-less" cooker to supply men in the trenches with hot drink and food, with Sgt. [uncertain] making a sketch to have it built tomorrow. | People: Col. Frith. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-17 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Cold weather of the past 3 days subsiding; 42 cases of infectious diseases in the isolation section; this has been the average for the past month. | Casualties: 42 infectious disease cases in isolation.

- **1915-11-19 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Tested the "fire-less cooker" — water at 205°F at 10.05 a.m. still 146.3°F at 1.20 p.m., 129.2°F at 2.45 p.m. and 109.4°F at 4.55 p.m., well above blood heat — visited Aldershot Camp vacated by the R.C.R., left in fair condition, and the Bulford well under construction had another setback, the earth caving in so the curb slipped, giving only 7½ ft of the 12 ft depth and 5½ ft diameter instead of 7, losing 1666 gallons of the 2827 asked for. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-19 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Major Munro in hospital with paratyphoid; weather cold again; the Aquitania arrives but did not take many cases from this hospital; reinforcements of 13 nursing sisters arrives on the Aquitania. | People: Major Munro. | Casualties: none.

Frith, also handed him a model of a camp stove made from an oil drum, decided a new well is to be started at Bulford Camp on Monday to develop a third water source — 12 ft deep, 8 ft diameter, 100 ft of gallery, with a tank and pump — and visited [uncertain] 15, where a case of measles had been taken a couple of days ago, finding a civilian child with measles in a house where 10 men were billeted, three of whom had not had measles and now look like septic sore throat but are recovering, recommending no more men be [uncertain] with them for 10 days. | People: Col. Frith. | Casualties: measles — a civilian child and three men with septic sore throat, recovering.

O.C. with Lt-Col Elder, Lt-Col McCrae and Capt. Lew inspected the Meerut Stationary Hospital at Boulogne. | People: Lt-Col J. M. Elder, Lt-Col J. McCrae, Capt. Lew.

- **1915-11-24 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Captain J. W. Hutchison returned from leave.
- **1915-11-25/26 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Fairly quiet on the front; Cpl A. Cameron #65147 received a slight shrapnel wound in the leg. | People: Cpl A. Cameron #65147 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 wounded

- **1915-11-25 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.

Frith and Col. Lindsay, the A.D.M.S. and D.A.D.M.S., at Bulford Camp to go over the water situation and disinfectors — the new well progressing, the disinfectors promised for a week from today. | People: Col. Frith, Col. Lindsay. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-11-28 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 sick horses. Evacuated 8 to No. 10 Veterinary Hospital, NEUFCHATEL. | People: No. 10 Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 2 horses received, 8 horses evacuated.
- **1915-11-28 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Sunday — kept all men at home, church parade, weather very cold, the coldest yet, ground frozen 3 inches and not thawing in daylight, and Col. Frith is getting one large and one small "fireless-Cooker" built after the section's plan for each battalion to try, with arrangements to supply Col. Lindsay two men for iron, glazing and carpentry jobs and to protect water pipes from frost. | People: Col. Frith, Col. Lindsay. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-28 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Twelve degrees of frost; water supply pipes frozen, cutting off water from the various departments.

- **1915-11-29 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Heavy downpour of rain with strong cold south-easterly gale; tents almost uninhabitable, roads almost impassable with mud; visit by Surgeon-General Woodhouse, D.M.S., L. of C., 11 a.m. | People: Surg-Gen Woodhouse.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 reinforcements from Canadian Veterinary Hospital, HAVRE. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Sent in reports and certificates on absence of cameras and roll-call on 28 November, sent an iron worker to protect water pipes at the Brasserie in [uncertain] from freezing, received a report from [uncertain] Major's inspection of C.M.R. care of [uncertain] below Bulford, reported not clean and ordered cleaned, and visited [uncertain] Officers Rest and [uncertain] Rest Station, then the A.D.M.S. in Bailleul; all going well in the unit. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — 623 patients in hospital, 157 cases frost bite; health of personnel good with the exception of 3 officers and 5 men; food and water satisfactory. | Casualties: 623 patients in hospital, 157 frostbite cases.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Heavy rains of yesterday continued throughout the night and early morning. Departmental reports appended to the volume: Dental (Capt. C. H. A. Stevenson) — 350 patients, 220 fillings, 150 extractions, 75 prophylaxis, 20 prosthetic, 19 July–31 October; X-Ray (Capts. Pirie and Wilkins) — 1,540 radiographs 8 August–5 November, two "Interruptless Transformer" machines, 23 good tubes; Sanitary (Capt. R. St. J. Macdonald) — camp site, water supply, excreta and sullage disposal, flies, disinfection; Medical (Lt-Col J. McCrae) — rheumatic fever, pneumonia, exanthems, enteric diseases, painful shins, chilblains/trench feet, neurasthenia, circulatory disturbances, malaria, dysentery, haemothorax. | People: Capt. C. H. A. Stevenson, Capt. L. H. Thornton, Capts. Pirie and Wilkins, Capt. R. St. J. Macdonald, Lt-Col J. McCrae.

Murray #67945 (25th Bn) shrapnel wounds in left chest, thigh, leg and foot, and Pte D. Drew #65282 (24th Bn) shrapnel wound in the right thigh. | People: Pte M. Murray #67945 (25th Bn); Pte D. Drew #65282 | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 wounded (one 25th Bn)
- **1915-12-01 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 3 sick horses. | Casualties: 3 horses received.

McConnell. | Casualties: 7 trench-feet cases seen, 2 of them severe.
- **1915-12-01 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Large influx of patients; 800 treated today due to frost bite cases (trench feet) following heavy rain and low temperature on the Peninsula on 27–29 November; different degrees of trench feet, from simple numbness to gangrene of toes and feet causing loss of the same. | Casualties: 800 treated today (trench feet / frostbite).
- **1915-12-01 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Capt. Colin Russel left for England to report as Neurologist at the Canadian Special Hospital, Granville Hotel, Ramsgate; Rontgen Society of London memorandum: Capt. A. Howard Pirie elected seventh honorary member (with Rontgen, Sir W. Crookes, Sir Oliver Lodge, Sir Ernest Rutherford, Professor Holznecht, Professor Stephen Leduc). | People: Capt. Colin Russel, Capt. A. Howard Pirie.
- **1915-12-02/03 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Our artillery maintained a heavy bombardment of enemy positions all day but drew little reply; Pte St Marie #65867 killed and Pte H. Robinson #21180 (5th Field Co., Canadian Engineers) slightly wounded in the scalp; new advanced first aid post opened at the head of the V.C. Road. | People: Pte St Marie #65867; Pte H. Robinson #21180 (5th Field Co., C. Engrs) | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 1 wounded | Locations: V.C. Road
- **1915-12-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 1 sick horse. | Casualties: 1 horse received.
- **1915-12-02 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Continued the camp inspection with Col Firth, finding many camps unnecessarily muddy and in need of drainage, and tried two cooks — one for absence from billet, one for drunkenness — letting both off on suspended sentence for good conduct. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-02 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Visited Col Firth about an efficiency test of a model fireless cooker made by the engineers and put suggestions for the men's comfort and morale, including "vitamines" and an apple a day in the diet, while Gen. Currie was writing to Gen. Carson to ask for more variety of food. | People: Col Firth, Gen. Currie, Gen. Carson, Capt. Mc[uncertain]. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-02 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-12-03/04 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Very quiet; alarm bell system finished in the Dressing Station and a code of signals arranged; D.A.D.M.S. visited the station and was well pleased; acetylene gas generator being made from two petrol drums to light the quarters. | People: D.A.D.M.S. [uncertain] | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Kemmel
- **1915-12-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 1 sick horse. Issued 1 cured. Evacuated 7 to No. 13 Veterinary Hospital, NEUFCHATEL. | People: No. 13 Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 1 horse received, 7 horses evacuated, 1 horse issued cured.
- **1915-12-03 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Completed the fireless cooker efficiency test, the water still 129.2° F after nearly 6 hours, visited the Bulford baths with the A.D.M.S., and lectured officers of the 1st and 10th Bns. on water precautions and "Salamander" carbon-monoxide poisoning, with Col Ross speaking on gases, trench-feet and hospital facilities. | People: Col Ross. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-03 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-12-04/05 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Rain, cold and windy; gas piping finished and a 10-gallon petrol drum installed; renewal of rifle and machine-gun fire; Pte [uncertain] J. #65955 killed, Pte Wee[uncertain] J. wounded in the wrist, and Pte [uncertain] R. #65252 bullet wound in the right thigh. | People: Pte [uncertain] J. #65955; Pte Wee[uncertain] J.; Pte [uncertain] R. #65252 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 2 wounded
- **1915-12-04 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 sick horses. | Casualties: 2 horses received.
- **1915-12-04 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Found the Bulford baths boiler leaking in all directions and ordered a replacement, and visited Koutepipe camp where Lt. J. A. Davison of the 15th Bn. was suffering from measles and had been isolated with 5 others, isolation to continue for 6 days. | People: Lt. J. A. Davison. | Casualties: measles — Lt. Davison and 5 others isolated.
- **1915-12-04 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Continuous downpours of rain for three days; lines almost impassable.
- **1915-12-05/06 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Cold and showery; at about 11 a.m. on the 6th the enemy shelled our HQ lines with some 30 shells, doing no damage; our artillery replied, dispersing an enemy working party and blowing in enemy trench parapets; a Royal Engineers officer blew up a counter mine; relieved by the 25th Battalion and proceeded to R.E. farms as Brigade Reserve; Pte Whiteford #66046 wounded in the shoulder. | People: Pte Whiteford #66046 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 wounded | Movement: trenches to R.E. farms (Brigade Reserve) | Locations: R.E. farms
- **1915-12-05 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Bailleul** — Maj. S. E. Powers reported to "Q" Branch of Canadian Corps and received instructions to report to Gen. Mercer and proceed with organizing and training the new company. | People: Maj. S. E. Powers; Gen. Mercer. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1915-12-05 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 1 sick horse. | Casualties: 1 horse received.
- **1915-12-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Visited Dranoutre, found the new Bulford boiler had arrived but civilians had repaired the old one so the new one was held in reserve, visited the 10th Bn., and tried and dismissed Pte. [uncertain] on a drunkenness charge on questionable evidence. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-05 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Instructions to detail 30 Nursing Sisters for temporary duty in England, 8 p.m.

- **1915-12-06 | 24th Battalion | France** — Relieved by the 25th Bn. and moved into Brigade Reserve at R.E. Farm. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: trenches to R.E. Farm | Locations: R.E. Farm (N 14 d. 9.7)
- **1915-12-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Bailleul** — Maj. Powers requested the names of proposed personnel from troops under Canadian Corps command. | People: Maj. S. E. Powers. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1915-12-06 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 5 sick horses. | Casualties: 5 horses received.
- **1915-12-06 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Received a leave pass until the 15th, with Capt. Lomer to take his place, saw the new Bulford disinfectors inspected by Gen. Currie and Gen. Alderson with lice killed and clothes coming out dry, and addressed the 16th Bn. at Hyde Park Corner on trench feet, gas helmets, "Salamander" precautions and the louse campaign during a bombardment. | People: Capt. Lomer, Gen. Currie, Gen. Alderson. | Casualties: none. | Movement: O.C. on leave 6–16 December.
- **1915-12-06 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Dysentery cases becoming markedly less, also jaundice; two hundred cases of trench feet in hospital; 2 cases of tetanus following frost bites, one fatal; all frost cases got the serum. | Casualties: 1 death (tetanus following frostbite); 200 trench-feet cases in hospital.
- **1915-12-06 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Orders for N.C.O.s and men of the final year in Medicine to hold themselves ready to proceed to England en route to Canada to complete their medical course at McGill University, Montreal.
- **1915-12-07 | 24th Battalion | France** — Visited by Maj. Gen. A.E.W. Turner V.C., C.B., D.S.O. | People: Maj. Gen. A.E.W. Turner | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: R.E. Farm (Brigade Reserve)
- **1915-12-07/10 | 24th Battalion | R.E. Farms, Belgium** — In billets; working parties daily; visit from Major General R. E. W. Turner V.C. C.B. D.S.O.; two companies attended baths at Westoutre; several hostile airships about on the morning of the 7th, our anti-aircraft guns active all day; sick parade held daily. | People: Maj Gen R. E. W. Turner | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: R.E. farms; Westoutre
- **1915-12-07 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Meteren** — Headquarters of the new company was established at Meteren (map ref. X17 C 3.4, Sheet 27 N.E.). | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Bailleul–Meteren.
- **1915-12-07 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 1 sick horse. | Casualties: 1 horse received.

- **1915-12-09 | 24th Battalion | France** — 175 men supplied for working parties in the Right and Left Sectors; two companies attended baths at Westoutre. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Westoutre

- **1915-12-16 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Reached Bailleul at 2 a.m. from leave, describing bullying, delays and too few life-belts on the leave journey, and found all had gone well in his absence except 2 men punished and a measles quarantine established among civilians at St Jans and [uncertain] Camp Farm, while Capt. Lomer had joined the unit. | People: Capt. Lomer. | Casualties: none (measles quarantine noted).

Smith #65901; Cpl Yolland #66090 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 died of wounds, 1 wounded | Movement: trenches to billets in Locre | Locations: Locre

Turner visited the battalion and gave his Christmas greetings to all ranks; at 4 p.m. the battalion moved to the trenches; drizzling rain; quiet on the front; no casualties. | People: Maj Gen R. E. - **1915-12-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — In rain and quiet guns, visited the front-line trenches of the 1st Bde. with the A.D.M.S., finding them badly drained with water in most dug-outs but clean and the men cheerful, visited [uncertain] patients who were not serious, and submitted a report praising the Expeditionary [uncertain] canteens. | Casualties: none serious.

- **1915-12-24 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — A suspected cerebro-spinal meningitis case was reported from 6th Cdn R., the spinal fluid clear with practically no polymorphonuclear cells and the culture negative, roads at food distribution points were flooded, mails delayed 3 days, and a man tried for insolence to an N.C.O. was made to apologize publicly before the unit. | Casualties: one suspected meningitis case, culture negative.
- **1915-12-24 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-12-25/26 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Fairly quiet along the front; in the afternoon the enemy made attempts to fraternize with our men; this was stopped and fire opened on them. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1915-12-25 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Passed a very quiet Christmas with hardly any gun firing, the men of the unit got up a dinner, and all avoidable fatigues were dispensed with. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-25 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — Progress of patients in hospital more satisfactory of late, due in a measure to fine weather and better food; Major Munro and Capt. - **1915-12-25 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Special dinners at the different messes; general routine duties dispensed with as far as possible.

Bourgeois #67244 (25th Bn); L/Cpl Northington #68333 (25th Bn) | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 died, 1 wounded (both 25th Bn)

Farm to Right Sector trenches
- **1916-03-26/27 | 24th Battalion | Right Sector, Kemmel, Belgium** — Night of 26/27 March: three scout patrols of three scouts each reconnoitred routes to the enemy wire for Bangalore torpedoes; one torpedo was successfully laid in the enemy wire in front of trench K1 and fired at 4.15 a.m.; the party for H4 trench was seen by the enemy and forced back with the torpedo; two attempts to place a torpedo opposite J3 Right trench failed, and a third attempt left the party in No Man's Land when the bombardment began — Scout F. Juteau (No. 41158) was killed making his way back, and Scout W. J. Dimmer (No. 6598) [also written "Dwyer" in the diary] was found by a scout patrol (Pte S. J. Bethune, No. 65077, and Pte E. C. Collins, No. 65192) sheltering in an old trench about 150 yards from the enemy wire and led safely back. | People: Scout F. Juteau No. 41158; Scout W. J. Dimmer No. 6598 [also written "Dwyer"]; Pte S. J. Bethune No. 65077; Pte E. C. Collins No. 65192 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed | Locations: K1; H4; J3 Right trench

- **1916-03-27 | 24th Battalion | Right Sector, Kemmel, Belgium** — Organized bombardment began at 4.15 a.m. in co-operation with a neighbouring operation; after the explosion of a mine on the left the enemy sent up flares, and four minutes later our artillery opened up, the enemy retaliating with heavies, trench mortars, grenades and field artillery forming a barrage behind the support trenches and heavily shelling the communication trenches until 6 a.m.; telephone communication between battalion headquarters and the trenches was broken at 5 a.m. and restored at 7.15 a.m.; casualties six wounded and one killed; the rest of the day unusually quiet. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 6 wounded

- **1916-05-01 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Voormezeele** — Two artillery positions, AP1 (I33 A31) and AP2 (I33 B3.6), each occupied by a gun and crew, damaged by hostile artillery fire between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m.: at AP1 the gun was put out of action and spare parts destroyed, at AP2 the front of the emplacement was blown in and the spare machine gun barrel damaged, the emplacement repaired immediately the shelling stopped; indirect fire used from I 32 D3.6, I 32 C 4.3 and the sunken road at O1 A 2.1 covering Hiele Farm, St. Eloi Road, Messines–St. Eloi Road and between Martins Farm; the machine gun at Sardine Box (I 32 A.2.1), manned by Borden's M.G. Battery, slightly damaged by fire at 10 p.m., and an alternative position manned by a gun from Voormezeele Reserve; Lieut. F. H. Duck and two O.R. reported at the Camiers Machine Gun School for a course of instruction; casualties: one O.R. killed and two O.R. wounded (total strength 9 officers, 147 O.R.). | People: Lieut. F. H. Duck. | Companies: Borden's M.G. Battery; Camiers Machine Gun School. | Casualties: **1 O.R. killed, 2 O.R. wounded (all unnamed)**.

Brigade — recommendations, gun positions, results 19 Apr–7 May. Dugout built in Sanctuary Wood left; three in right sector; bombproof ammunition store built; Hooge Crater dugout ready if cooperation between brigades had been more in evidence; sandbag work for other brigades; parapets for firing mortars and a grenade parapet. Complaints: Light mortars need permission to fire while Divisional (Medium) mortars fire without; a 49th Battalion commander claimed 17 casualties through mortars (Horan believed the Divisional people had not fired); ammunition requisitioned independently by each brigade; waders not passed between brigades; separate reserve stores. | People: Capt. - **1916-05-14 to 1916-06-01 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Right Sector / Sanctuary Wood / Maple Copse / Zillebeke, Belgium** — Batteries into Right Sector and Sanctuary Wood. Dispositions: Right sector crew; Sanctuary Wood officer and crew; Maple Copse Sgt. Major [uncertain] gun crew with 4 Stokes ready; Zillebeke Village gun crew and extra men in reserve; other Battery back in Rest Camp relieving about 22 May. Guns: Stokes, 2 × 4" R.M.L and 3 × 3.7s. Orders kept Stokes 1,000 yds back of front line except when firing, making prompt retaliation and registering almost impossible. At end of month 3 officers went to Stokes Gun Course. Relieved 1 June; as German attack took place 2–3 June, both batteries stood ready for action. | Locations: Sanctuary Wood; Maple Copse; Zillebeke Village.

- **1916-06-01 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | B Camp, Belgium** — Day spent in field work and range practice; early morning enemy planes which dropped bombs on Poperinghe were fired on by our guns, range extreme and not effective. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1916-06-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Connaught and Patricia Lines** — Inspected Connaught and Patricia Lines in the morning, finding conditions good. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Field** — At a meeting of the Corps Water Board in the afternoon, details for the extension of the water system were discussed, with no shortage as yet. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-06-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — Heavy shelling beginning at 8.30 a.m. was followed by a German attack, front-line trenches in the right sector were in enemy possession by 4 p.m., and lines were maintained with difficulty under intense bombardment. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | St Sylvestre-Cappel** — Received one 3-ton lorry, transferred off one 30-Cwt lorry; feeding strength as issued at railhead — Divisional Troops 4,665 men, 3,394 horses; 7th Bde. 5,369 men, 542 horses; 8th Bde. 5,361 men, 541 horses; 9th Bde. 5,801 men, 598 horses. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — General look round and piles of correspondence; a case was remanded for F.G.C.M.; heavy bombardment and unconfirmed wild rumours from the night before. | People: — | Companies: Headquarters Company. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi Front** — Officers and N.C.O.s spent considerable time reconnoitring their front; under cover of artillery fire the following points were registered: No 2 Crater, Piccadilly Fm., and the sap head at O.3.b.7.1. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | A.P.1 / Hill Top / Lock Post / Spoil Bank / Convent School** — Work at A.P.1, Hill Top, Lock Post and Spoil Bank continued, good progress being made; the 26th Battalion supplying a work party of 8 men each night; a sentry box started and partly completed at Convent School; all guns, spare parts and ammunition gone over and thoroughly cleaned. | People: — | Companies: 26th Battalion. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | B Camp / E Camp, Belgium** — 10 a.m. while parading for inspection by G.O.C., message arrives to prepare to move at 1 hour's notice; warned to move at once, ordered to Camp E and await orders; left Camp B 3.30 p.m.; D.A.D.O.S. leave 8 guns in their hands, take only 8 guns to advance; operation order No. 19 received: move 4 guns to occupy 4 positions in Lille Road; A Section moved 6 p.m. and in position 2 hours later; C Section ready to move at short notice; 9 p.m. B.H.Q. and M.G.C. H.Q. move to Chateau Belge. | Companies: A Section; C Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: B Camp to E Camp to Chateau Belge.
- **1916-06-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe S.** — Evacuated to No. 13 Vety Hospital Neufchatel 18 horses, Eleven of these are skin disease cases — Corpl. Southern in charge of Conducting party — Acquittance Roll No. 51 Forwarded to Paymaster 3rd Echelon Col. Watson D.V.S. and Major Sutcliffe A.D.V.S. inspects the section today. Weekly Ration state Present Strength Report and Weekly Offence Report rendered to AA+QMG. — The following reports were rendered to A.D.V.S — (Mobile Veterinary Section A.F.A. 2000 — Weekly Mange state — Class Animals and Horses collected from inhabitants — Hdqts Divsl — Artillery and Signal Coy. Hdqts — AFA-2000 — Weekly Mange state and classification of Animals. | People: Corpl. Southern; Col. Watson; Major Sutcliffe. | Casualties: 18 horses evacuated. | Movement: Sent to Aa.

- **1916-06-03 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — Bombardment and fighting continued, forward lines in the left sector were good, the right sector was in from noon until 4 p.m., and divisional lines to the Right Brigade were out for forty minutes in the afternoon while lateral communication kept divisional headquarters in touch. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-03–1916-06-05 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | St Sylvestre-Cappel** — Issued supplies as usual. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

Mercer. | Companies: No. 9 Field Ambulance; Headquarters Company. | Casualties: none in the Train; Gen. Mercer killed (reported 3 June).
- **1916-06-03 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi Front** — A new system of relief tried out in the right sector: battery split into day and night shifts, an N.C.O. and four men for two guns. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | A.P.1 / Hill Top / Lock Post / Spoil Bank / Convent School** — The saps at A.P.1, Hill Top, Lock Post and Spoil Bank advanced a distance of 3 feet and timbered; the work party promised by the 26th Battalion unable to come owing to a stand to, so the work was carried on by the company's own men; a trench dug from the Convent School emplacement connecting it with the main trench; at M.G. Headquarters a surface dugout started and the roof braced up with timber. | People: — | Companies: 26th Battalion. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-03 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | —** — Covering letter from Capt. H. J. Horan (52nd Canadian Inf. Battalion) to Capt. R. C. Lalor, for A.A.G., Canadian Section, 3rd Echelon, G.H.Q., enclosing the synoptical diary 15 Mar–18 Jun 1916; unable to render a complete diary owing to ignorance of Circular 7 Feb 1916 (A-27-157-2A); circular letter handed to Mr. Ryerson, O.C. C-9-1 & 2. | People: Capt. H. J. Horan; Capt. R. C. Lalor; Lieut. J. E. Ryerson.
- **1916-06-03 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Chateau Belge / Ypres, Belgium** — 1 a.m. B.H.Q. moves to Ypres Ramparts; 2 a.m. C Section reports Ypres and despatched to be held in reserve at the Bund, I 21 b; 9 a.m. D Section reports Ypres with 4 guns from ordnance, one gun into emplacement in Ramparts, remainder kept under cover in Ypres; 8 men of A Section sent to 7th Bde. M.G.C. at Halfway House to replace casualties; communication trenches heavily shelled all day; enemy aeroplanes busy; 7.15 p.m. enemy bombardment begins in Sanctuary Wood and a feint made on our lines in Lovers Walk; 7.30 p.m. D Section 4 guns moved from Ypres to Lille Road; 8.30 p.m. 4 guns from Bund advanced to form new line of defence from I 22 d.4.6 north to I 16 a 7.8; 10 p.m. 2 guns of B Section under Lieut. Cordingly reported Bund and ordered by 8th B. M.G.C. to go to Zillebeke; C Section withdrawn from new line to relieve 8th B. M.G.C. | People: Lieut. Cordingly. | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section; 7th Bde. M.G.C.; 8th B. M.G.C. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Chateau Belge to Ypres; Ypres to Lille Road; Bund to Zillebeke.
- **1916-06-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — O.C. completes morning inspection of Hdqts Divisional horses. A.D.V.S visits section today — Ten horses admitted to M.V.S. | Casualties: 10 horses received.
- **1916-06-03 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Patricia and Connaught Lines** — With the Camp Commandant, went over Patricia and Connaught Lines, where ablution water from ponds was becoming very dirty and wells near the ponds were suggested, with green tops being put in. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-03 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Salonica** — Week ending 3 June: admissions 64, discharges 165, 1 death; health of the unit good; weather getting hot and dry. | Casualties: 1 death.

Graves detailed to the Central Medical Inspection Room. | People: Asst-Matron S. M. Hoerner, Capt W. G. McNevin, Capt C. A. Graves.
- **1916-06-04 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — Mutual bombardment continued intermittently, many lines were cut, and lines were laid for the 3rd Imperial Divisional Artillery, who moved up into this area. | People: — | Companies: 3rd Imperial Divisional Artillery | Casualties: none | Movement: 3rd Imperial Divisional Artillery moved up into this area
- **1916-06-04 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — The Adjutant and Mr McDonald attended a court martial; a private was placed under arrest for coming into the billet drunk; church parade for the Train at Headquarters Company parade ground. | People: Mr McDonald; Charlie. | Companies: Headquarters Company. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-04 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi Front** — Germans more active than usual with their trench mortars; retaliation by one Stokes mortar firing into crater 4 and artillery on their T.M. positions near Piccadilly Fm soon silenced them; Lt Johnstone [uncertain], 5½ Battery, and two N.C.O.s returned from the Stokes gun course at Terdeghem. | People: Lt Johnstone [uncertain] | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-04 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | A.P.1 / Hill Top / Lock Post / Spoil Bank** — Good progress at A.P.1, Hill Top, Lock Post and Spoil Bank, but owing to the unrest in this part of the line no work parties could be obtained from the battalions, and every available man in the company was used. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-04 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Enemy artillery very active on Zillebeke Village and communication trenches; 7.15 p.m. heavy barrage put on at Zillebeke Village and a feint made on Lovers Walk; Lieut. Lawson; Col. Simson. | Companies: 8th Brigade; 7th Brigade; No. 2 Company; No. 3 Company; No. 4 Company; Headquarters Company; Field Coys., Engineers, Pioneer & Composite Battalions. | Casualties: none | Movement: 8th Brigade and No. 3 Company to Steenvoorde.

Company (Imperials), who took over this portion of the line, and the company returned to rest billets. | People: — | Companies: 9th Brigade M.G. Company (Imperials). | Casualties: none | Movement: Relieved by 9th Brigade M.G. Company (Imperials); returned to rest billets.
- **1916-06-05 to 1916-06-15 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Zillebeke Bund / S.P. 16 / Maple Copse / Dormy House, Belgium** — Evening orders to proceed with 4 Stokes guns to Zillebeke Bund (4 gun crews, 2 officers); awaited orders two days; two guns and ammunition taken up to S.P. 16 near Maple Copse in anticipation of an attack. Nothing of moment. 11 June Mr. Ryerson ordered up with two crews as relief; on the way up received instructions covering attack of 10th–11th June. More ammunition brought up but rain for over 24 hours before the attack, no shelter for ammunition, fields impracticable for firing. 13 June relief went up to Dormy House, S.P. 16 having become untenable. 15 June orders to retire to Divisional Rest with the Brigade. | People: Lieut. J. E. Ryerson. | Locations: Zillebeke Bund; S.P. 16; Maple Copse; Dormy House.
- **1916-06-05 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Heavy artillery duel most of day; Zillebeke heavily bombarded; evening fairly quiet; 1 man suffering from shellshock evacuated. | Casualties: 1 O.R. evacuated (shellshock). | Movement: —
- **1916-06-05 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — O.C. completes morning inspection Billeting Papers amounting to 8 Francs and 5 Centimes was forwarded to B.R.O. Second Army. Poperinghe Ten Cars for shipment of horses tomorrow — Ambulance calls at Can. Cycl. Battalion and returns with Case No. 2044. | Casualties: 45 horses received, 3 mules received.
- **1916-06-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Dickeybusch Huts** — Dickeybusch Huts were being shelled, the majority of shells falling around the incinerator, which from an aeroplane might look like a howitzer, but the camp was empty, the troops having moved up, and convalescents were set to clean up, while Scottish and Dominion Lines were also empty and the Camp Commandant had returned to [uncertain]. | Casualties: none (camp empty).
- **1916-06-05 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Captains C. A. Graves and H. K. McKim returned from leave; convoy of 53 patients at 10.15 p.m. | People: Capt C. A. Graves, Capt H. K. Neilson, Capt F. G. Logie, Capt L. H. McKim.
- **1916-06-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — Increased activity and severe shelling put practically every circuit except the six-foot buried route out several times, and 1,218 telegrams and despatches were handled, the largest day's business since the beginning of operations. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | St Sylvestre-Cappel** — On account of the 9th Bde. coming into billets near Steenvoorde for reorganization, a dump was started at K.32.D.6.4, sheet 27, the lorries drawing supplies from railhead. | People: — | Companies: 9th Bde. | Casualties: none | Movement: New dump started at K.32.D.6.4.

- **1916-06-06 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi** — The 4-in mortars in the right half did good work firing on the German T.M. which were active in the evening; Lt Wayfield [uncertain] from 3rd Bde T.M. - **1916-06-08–1916-06-11 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — All lines were handed over to the 2nd Canadian Division Signal Company and maintained satisfactorily for them, a working party of 350 men was supplied, the proposed buried route from Doll's House to Ramparts (Ypres) was completed in four nights, and nine casualties were suffered from shellfire. | People: — | Companies: 2nd Canadian Division Signal Company | Casualties: 9 casualties from shellfire
- **1916-06-08 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | St Sylvestre-Cappel** — Received 12 men as reinforcements to complete establishment, the Ambulances of the Division having had a number of casualties; supplies unloaded and issued as usual. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: A number of casualties among the Divisional Ambulances (number not given).

- **1916-06-09 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Trenches near Zillebeke** — Left sector guns: 2 in Square Wood covering Armagh House and front line, 2 in support trench in rear of Rudkin House; those in Square Wood heavily shelled, two bomb stores blown up; decided to site guns in front line behind Armagh Wood. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-09 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke** — General reconnaissance of the Zillebeke area by all officers of the company. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-09 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Heavy artillery duelling continues; our artillery bombardment growing very intense; field batteries near Bund and Ypres subjected to heavy shell fire nearly all day; B.H.Q. at Bund heavily bombarded, brigade staff removed headquarters to Ypres; 2 O.R. wounded, 1 accidentally wounded while opening a beef can. | Casualties: 3 O.R. wounded (2 + 1 accidental). | Movement: —
- **1916-06-09 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Evacuated to No 13. Veterinary Hospital Neufchatel 18 horses. | People: No. 48578 Pte. Bilot C.G; Corpl. Ballinger. | Casualties: 30 horses received, 18 horses evacuated. | Movement: Sent to A.A.
- **1916-06-09 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Honorary Captain & Chaplain R. W. Ridgeway proceeded to 2nd Army Headquarters and was struck off the strength; Honorary Captain & Chaplain R. D. Harrison reported for duty and was taken on the strength. | People: Hon. Capt R. W. Ridgeway, Hon. Capt R. D. Harrison.
- **1916-06-10 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — The S.S.O. went to conference; the O.C. took S.S. Petrie; Anthony. | Companies: 3rd Imperial R.F.A. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-10 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Trenches near Zillebeke** — The G.O.C. objected to the Stokes being kept in front for fear of being captured, so a position near Knoll Farm was taken up, covering part of the front line, Square Wood and Foss Way C.T.; shelling during night and day very heavy in retaliation for artillery activity. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-10 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Field** — Trench stores at each emplacement completed to 10,000 S.A.A., 20 iron rations, 9 gallons of fresh water and 24 Mills bombs; intense bombardment by our artillery from 6:30 p.m. until 7 p.m. on the enemy's front line, with very heavy come back by the enemy. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-10 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund / Ypres, Belgium** — Ypres, Bund and communication trenches receive intense bombardment from early morning till night; calmer in evening and transport unmolested; no casualties. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-10 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — General Store — Col. Wilson and Major Sutcliffe inspects the section today — admitted 6 horses to M.V.S. today. | People: Col. Wilson; Major Sutcliffe. | Casualties: 6 horses received.
- **1916-06-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Abele** — At Abele for [uncertain]; paid the men. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-10 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Salonica** — Week ending 10 June: admissions 215, discharges 138. | Casualties: none recorded.
- **1916-06-10 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Convoy of 45 patients at 6.30 p.m.

- **1916-06-11 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Trenches near Zillebeke** — Relieved by 2nd T.M. Battery (4 guns) and 3rd T.M. - **1916-06-11 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Piccadilly Square** — Intense bombardment by our artillery on the Germans' front line from 2 a.m. to 2:30 a.m., practically no come back by the enemy; the company relieved in the evening by the 2nd Brigade M.G. Company; Lieut. Thomas wounded at 7 p.m. by shrapnel at Piccadilly Square. | People: Lieut. Thomas. | Companies: 2nd Brigade M.G. Company. | Casualties: **Lieut. Thomas — wounded by shrapnel at Piccadilly Square**. | Movement: Relieved by 2nd Brigade M.G. Company.
- **1916-06-11 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Heavy artillery duel throughout the day with periods of intense bombardment; 1 nervous breakdown. | Casualties: 1 O.R. nervous breakdown. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-11 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — AFB 213 and Location Report rendered to A.A.+ Q.M.G. Mobile Veterinary Section — admitted 5 horses to M.V.S. | People: No. 1278 Pte McRae J. | Casualties: 5 horses received, 5 horses issued cured.
- **1916-06-11 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Field** — Kit inspection and muster parade. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-11 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1916-06-12 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — The 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade, withdrawn and reinforced, went back into the line and had a successful attack recovering most of the ground lost on 2 June, all communications forward [uncertain — "dis"?] to headquarters office, and this Company was still maintaining lines for the Second Division. | People: — | Companies: 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 2nd Canadian Division Signal Company | Casualties: none | Movement: 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade went back into the line
- **1916-06-12 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | St Sylvestre-Cappel** — 1 30-Cwt L.G.O.C. lorry sent to base as casualty; received 1 30-Cwt L.G.O.C. lorry; supplies as usual. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 L.G.O.C. lorry (mechanical casualty).
- **1916-06-12 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Poperinghe** — The Adjutant and M.O. went to Poperinghe; Capt. Oliphant was instructed to join Headquarters Company to learn the ropes before Maj. Webb leaves to take command of 4th Train. | People: Capt. Oliphant; Maj. Webb. | Companies: Headquarters Company; 4th Train. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-12 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill 60 & Zillebeke** — Canadians again lost trenches at Zillebeke; guns parked on limber borrowed from the 5th Brigade M.G.
