- **1916-06-12 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Camp A Area 3 / Reninghelst** — Arrived at Camp A Area 3 at 5 a.m., had breakfast and rested the remainder of the day; the company moved off again at 5 p.m. to its rest billets at Reninghelst. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Camp A Area 3–Reninghelst (rest billets).
- **1916-06-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Violent artillery duels all day with periods of intense bombardment of German front line and flanks; orders for assault issued; ordered to obtain fire effect on German old lines; one gun advanced to S.P. 17 for enfilade fire on Loop and Birdcage, one gun at Dormy House for indirect fire on Birdcage trenches, one gun from Tuilerie for indirect fire on German support line in front of trenches 59, 60, 61, one gun at Zillebeke Switch for fire on Tor Top and German old line, all to open fire at 1.20 a.m. 13 June; no casualties. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-12 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Billeting papers amounting to 8 Francs was forwarded to B.R.O. Second Army — A.D.V.S. Poperinghe Four cars for the shipment of horses tomorrow admitted Four horse to M.V.S. | Casualties: 4 horses received.
- **1916-06-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Scottish Lines** — At Scottish Lines, made Cpl. Killen [uncertain], with Cpl. Oram and [uncertain] [uncertain] of [uncertain] without pay while in charge of lines. | People: Cpl. Killen, Cpl. Oram. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-12 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Captain C. C. Main posted to No. 13 Stationary Hospital for temporary duty; convoys of 49 patients at 1.30 a.m., 20 at 6 p.m. and 45 at 10.30 p.m. | People: Capt C. C. Main.
- **1916-06-13–1916-06-14 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — Nothing to report on a quiet front, with test stations and lines strengthened and repaired. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1916-06-13 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Field** — Guns, ammunition and spare parts thoroughly cleaned and belts refilled; kit inspection held and deficiencies made up; foot inspection held. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — 12.45 a.m. after a quiet spell violent bombardment of German front line begins; 1.30 a.m. attack launched on Mount Sorrel, Hill 61, Hill 62, and a bomb attack by a battalion of 9th Canadian Brigade on Hill 56, Rigo St. and the old front line along Warrington Ave and Byland Ave; several prisoners made; on Hill 62 machine guns survived the bombardment and held up the attack, had to be bombed from the flanks; recommendation that deep dugouts be made for all M.G. emplacements advanced in front of front line; no casualties. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-13 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Evacuated to No. 13 Vety Hospital Neufchatel 22 Horses today Corpl. Ambulance leaves for the Cavalry Barracks Ypres for to bring in a badly Wounded case. | People: Corpl. Southern. | Casualties: 1 horse received, 23 horses evacuated.
- **1916-06-13 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Dickeybusch Huts** — Dickeybusch Huts were empty, so a sergeant and six men were sent to act as guard there, while [uncertain] camps nearby were pulling down and removing huts. | Casualties: none.

Capt A. J. Labonte, Maj E. W. Archibald.

- **1916-06-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — Leave for the Train was cut to two per week; a jibbing horse of No. 4 Company was cast; casualties were reported pretty heavy over the last two days, and a German wounded prisoner was reported to have said "God damn the Kaiser". | People: Maj. - **1916-06-29 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Half Way House / S.P. 16 / R.S. 8, Belgium** — 6.30 P.M. 3 officers and 25 O.R. marched to Half Way House; 4 guns + equipment by transport. Took over positions, dugouts, etc. held by 7th Canadian Trench Mortar Battery: 1 officer, 1 crew with 1 gun in S.P. 16; 1 gun + crew in R.S. 8; 2 guns, 1 officer and 10 O.R. in Half Way House. Trenches held extend from Menin Road (Sh. 28 I 7 B 3.8, and Culvert I 19 A 1.7) to Sh. 28 I 24 D 7.7. Night quiet. No casualties. 9th Bde. M.G. Co. relieved 7th M.G.C. in same sector. | Companies: 7th Canadian Trench Mortar Battery; 9th Bde. M.G. Machine Gun Company. | Casualties: 2 O.R. wounded. | Movement: B Camp to Zillebeke Bund.

- **1916-06-30 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — The S.S.O. went to D.D. of S. & T.; the O.C. visited the dentist; news of Sir Roger Casement gave great satisfaction. | People: Sir Roger Casement. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-30 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Spoil Bank** — The saps at Spoil Bank started again and work progressing very fast, as two sappers were obtained from the 25th Battalion; everything in this sector very quiet all day. - **1916-06-30 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Very quiet with exception of a little counter battery work; information that he is building trenches which are demolished by British fire last night; 9th Canadian Brigade relieves 7th C. AFA 2000 Mange state — Animal Class Horses collected from inhabitants and Animals died or destroyed — Hdqts Divsl — Artillery Signal Coy. and Engineers A.F.A. 2000 Weekly Mange state and Animal Class. - **1916-06-30 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Devonshire Lines** — The camp at G 22, called Devonshire Lines, had buildings nearly completed, latrines built, [uncertain] being dug, and an incinerator under way. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Salonica** — There were 22 admissions of the personnel during the month, eleven being due to diarrhoea; 7 men remaining in hospital on 30 June. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-06-30 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Convoys of 62 patients at 4 p.m. and 65 at 9.45 p.m.

- **1916-07-01 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — The O.C. served as a member of a General Court Martial and the Adjutant as Judge Advocate; at the ground sports the 3rd Train took 2 firsts and 4 seconds; aeroplanes were very active. | People: — | Companies: 1st Train; 3rd Train; Headquarters Company. | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-01 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi** — On the left sector 321 rounds fired in support of the raid, and on the night 89 rounds; casualties: No. 61530 Pte G. Trembly wounded, No. 67454 Sgt G. E. Roche wounded, No. 65481 Cpl J. Innis killed. | People: Pte G. Trembly, Sgt G. E. Roche, Cpl J. Innis | Companies: — | Casualties: Cpl J. Innis killed; Pte G. - **1916-07-01 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Voormezeele, Belgium** — G.S.O.3 from 2nd Canadian Division inspected Hqrs and emplacements; 1 officer and 3 O.R. left for Vickers M.G. Course at Camiers; lack of material still exists at Spoil Bank; 2 officers and 3 O.R. expected back from course at Camiers. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-01 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | S.P. 16 / Hill 57, Belgium** — Battery still in trenches as on 30 June. Day: no firing or work. Night: 1 gun crew from Half-Way House relieved crew at S.P. 16. Lieuts. Reade and Ryerson reconnoitred Hill 57 and vicinity (I 24 B 2 3) for a position to build a defensive emplacement; suitable location found. Crews improving emplacements and cover. No firing. | People: Lieut. Reade; Lieut. J. E. Ryerson. | Locations: S.P. 16; Hill 57; Half-Way House. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-01 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Our batteries shelled quite heavily throughout the day; aeroplanes very active on both sides; five of our planes returning from reconnaissance met two German planes and one was seen to fall; one M.G. gun at Culvert knocked out by German shell, 3 O.R. wounded. | Casualties: 3 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —
- **1916-07-01 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — War Diary for month of June Forwarded to A.D.V.S. Ambulance calls at 1st Bde. 4th Batty and returns with case No. 2287 Corpl. Ballinger returns from St. Omer brought a receipt for 64 Horses the original party was 66 but an accident happened 4 Kilometres this side of Steenvoorde Case No. 2180 slipped into a ditch and broke his leg. the Vet. Sgt at No. 3 Horse Halt returned and destroyed it. | People: No. 2287 Corpl. Ballinger. | Casualties: 3 horses received.
- **1916-07-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Dickeybusch** — Inspected camps and billets between Belgian Cafe and Dickeybusch, where the 3rd Pioneers, Engineers and Artillery were all in good shape. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-01 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Salonica** — Matron Charleson invalided to England; admissions 188, discharges 221, 281 in hospital; weather very hot all the week; two deaths. | People: Matron Charleson. | Casualties: 2 deaths.

- **1916-07-02 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | New Bond St. / Roslyn Rd. / Regent St. / Culvert, Belgium** — Day: no firing or work. Night: took over 33 rds. Ammu. 3" Stokes left in trench 71 [uncertain] by 7th Can. T.M.B. Lieut. Ryerson with 1 Corpl [uncertain] + 1 man reconnoitred New Bond St., Roslyn Rd., Regent St. to the Culvert and Trenches 6 B to 74 (I 17 b-d – I 18 A-c). District unsuitable for Stokes mortars: enemy trenches out of range for offensive operations, ground in front very low, wet and badly cut up by shell fire; unlikely enemy would attack there, so defensive positions hardly necessary. Whole ground under observation by day. No firing. | People: Lieut. J. E. Ryerson. | Locations: New Bond St.; Roslyn Rd.; Regent St.; Culvert. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-02 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Hostile shelling on Lille Gate Rd, Shrapnel Corner and transport routes in retaliation for our artillery activity; inter-section relief took place 11 p.m.; enemy very quiet but very nervous especially north and south; 1 officer and 4 O.R. reported back from Vickers course. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-07-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Ambulance calls at 7th Belgium Artillery 1st Batty and returns with case No. 2247. AFB-213 and Location report was rendered to A.A.+Q.M.G. Admitted 18 horses to M.V.S. today. | Casualties: 18 horses received.

- **1916-07-03 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi** — Stokes gun successful in stopping hostile bombing. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Voormezeele, Belgium** — Parapet at S.P.8, in very poor condition, repaired with some 300 sandbags; sap at Lock Post cleaned out and advanced 4 feet; work continued on emplacement at Ecluse 8 with over 200 sandbags filled and put in position; frames for holding gas blankets being erected at all emplacements and dug-outs; progress on all work very slow for want of material; indirect fire by one gun for 2 hours. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-03 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Culvert / Hill St. / Half-Way House / S.P. 16, Belgium** — Day: no firing or work. Instructions from Bde. Major, 9th Can. Inf. Bde., to put 1 Stokes mortar at Culvert and one in Hill St., digging them in temporarily and commencing proper emplacements. 10.00 P.M. Lt. McKenzie left Half-Way House with crew of 1 NCO, 3 men, 1 × 3" Stokes mortar and carrying party of 1 NCO, 15 men with 51 rounds Stokes ammunition, proceeding to Culvert; mortar set up in temporary open emplacement, ammunition under cover, mortar taken into men's shelter at daybreak. 10.00 P.M. Lt. Reade with crew of 1 NCO, 3 men left S.P. 16 with 1 Stokes mortar for Hill St.; mortar set up in temporary open emplacement; position at S.P. 16 abandoned, crew camping some 20 yds to Hill St. during the night. | People: Lt. McKenzie; Lt. Reade. | Locations: Culvert; Hill St.; Half-Way House; S.P. 16. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-03 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Quiet during most of day; our artillery bombarded Mount Sorrel 3 p.m. with very little retaliation; increase in machine gun fire and rifle very marked. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-07-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Billeting Papers amounting to 7 Francs 50 Centimes was forwarded to Second Army Hdqtrs. O.C. Visits the ADVS - admitted 32 horses to MVS. today - 20 of these belong to 7th Belgium Artillery. | Casualties: 32 horses received.

- **1916-07-04 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill St. / Culvert / Halfway House, Belgium** — Day: no firing. Site selected in Hill St. for defensive emplacement. [uncertain] officer refused to allow any work building emplacement for Stokes mortar for fear of indicating to enemy that position was occupied. - **1916-07-04 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Quiet during day but machine gun and rifles very active at night; work on new Dormy Lane position started; area south of Zillebeke Bund very heavily shelled 7 p.m.; 2nd Canadian Bde. on our right and 60th Division on our left. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-07-04 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — Ambulance calls at 7th Batt. 2nd Inf. - **1916-07-08 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Voormezeele, Belgium** — Work continued on dug-out at Y.4 and sap at A.P.1 advanced 4 feet and timbered; indirect-fire emplacement at Sunken Road pushed into the bank 6 feet and well sandbagged, with a slit made as protection against shell fire; work on Hdqrs indirect-fire emplacement commenced, dug down 3 feet with communication trench made; reinforcements of 1 officer arrived. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-08 to 1916-07-09 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill St. / Culvert / Trench #61 / Forrester Lane, Belgium** — Night 8/9 July: 44 rounds fired from Hill St.; firing ceased 12.00 A.M. promptly. Bombing officer of 58th Battn., in trench at junction of old front line + Darlington [uncertain], observed fire and reported it well directed and placed, searching bombing post and vicinity and enfilading trench #61 (old); bombing post unoccupied on arrival of bombing party of 58th Battn.; ground in vicinity badly cut up. 11.45 P.M. Stokes mortar in Culvert opened fire on old bombing post No. 8 (Hooge) and trench on either side, mortar being traversed gradually. 12.00 A.M. fire directed on trench at head of Forrester Lane. 12.00 [as written] ceased fire. 40 rounds in all fired. Bombing officer of 52nd Battn. reported old bombing post #8 badly broken up and scarcely recognizable, unoccupied on his arrival. Results of setting up guns at night by compass from bearings obtained from maps more satisfactory than anticipated. No casualties sustained. Splinter-proof cover most valuable. | People: bombing officers of 58th and 52nd Battalions. | Companies: 58th Battalion; 52nd Battalion. | Locations: Hill St.; Culvert; Trench #61; Forrester Lane; Hooge. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-08 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill St. / Culvert / Halfway House, Belgium** — 5.30 P.M. Lieut. Ryerson received verbal instructions from B.Gen. Hill, Brigadier 9th Can. Inf. Bde. (confirmed by 9th Can. Inf. Bde. Operation Order 25) regarding operations night 8/9 July. Stokes mortars in Hill St. and Culvert to be used, although neither emplacement complete. Temporary splinter-proof cover hurriedly erected over Hill St. emplacement, hole left just large enough for discharge of shell. 7.00 P.M. Lieut. Reade given charge of Hill St. gun. 44 rounds [uncertain] prepared at Halfway House and carried by reserve men to gun position, all available red or long-range cartridges being used. 9.00 P.M. Lt. Ryerson left Halfway House for Culvert to give detailed instructions to Lt. MacDonald, in charge of operations there. Carrying party arranged to carry ammunition from Halfway House to Culvert as supply was low — 45 rounds carried. 11.45 P.M. Stokes mortar in Hill St. (I 24 B 2 1/2 1 1/2) opened fire on enemy bombing post in old front line trench #61 and from J 19 A 0 2 1/2 to J 19 A 7 2. Range 360 to 380 yards. | People: Lieut. J. E. Ryerson; B.Gen. Hill; Lieut. Reade; Lt. MacDonald. | Locations: Hill St.; Culvert; Halfway House. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-08 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Quiet in morning; in afternoon batteries were shelled; heavy bombardment of Mount Sorrel by our artillery for fifteen minutes at 7.15 p.m.; we opened an intensive bombardment at 11.45 followed by an attack; 5 O.R. casualties including one sergeant killed; Lieut. L. Ellis reported for duty from Machine Gun Base. | People: Lieut. L. Ellis. | Casualties: 5 O.R. casualties, including 1 sergeant killed. | Movement: —

[uncertain] Sydney - Have found it necessary to destroy Case 2316 - Belonging to A Sqdn 2nd Troop Canadian Cavalry [uncertain] Regiment - Post Mortem revealed Rupture of the Flexor [uncertain] Off Hock. | People: Corpl. - **1916-07-23 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Steenvoorde area, France** — 9.00 A.M./12.00 [uncertain] men attached given [uncertain] practise in firing live ammunition. Lieut. MacDonald and 3 Corporals returned from Trench Mortar School, Terdeghem. Model emplacement tested out to see what traverse could be obtained: emplacement 6'×6' with floor 8' below surface, aperture 2'×3' in roof for discharge of shell; allowed traverse sufficient to bombard 100 yds of trench supposing emplacement 200 yds behind front line. On examination of craters, total traverse of mortar at 300 yards is LESS than at 200 yds., whereas various Trench Mortar Schools including 2nd Army school at Terdeghem teach traverse at 300 yards is 50% greater than at 200 yards. | People: Lieut. MacDonald. | Locations: Terdeghem. | Casualties: none.

Enemy obtained direct hit with about 7.7 [uncertain] on ammunition dug-out in Hill St., doing slight damage — broke boxes containing Stokes bombs but did not detonate any. Left sector: [uncertain] mortar in Crab Crawl fired [uncertain] 6 rounds in retaliation to rifle grenades. 6.00 P.M. [uncertain] fired 3 rounds registration; 9.00 P.M. 6 rounds retaliation. Day quiet. Casualties nil. | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Hill St.; Crab Crawl. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-07-28 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Mount Sorrel / Crab Crawl, Belgium** — 1.30 A.M. mortars in Mount Sorrel fired 25 rounds on enemy front line in retaliation to whizz-bangs. Enemy immediately ceased fire. 5.00 P.M. mortar in Crab Crawl fired 3 rounds registration. 10.00 P.M. ditto 6 rounds retaliation to rifle grenades. 11.00 P.M. mortars in Mount Sorrel fired 20 rounds in retaliation to about 10 T.M. bombs. Casualties nil. Our patrols went out + we were obliged to cease fire. Gun No. 6 from R.S. 8 taken to Mount Sorrel, where it will be of more use — a third emplacement available there, slightly damaged by a shell about a week ago, easily put in usable shape. [Remarks: patrol report — enemy M.G. put out of action, catching crews during a relief + causing several casualties.] | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Crab Crawl; R.S. 8. | Casualties: none (battery).

In early evening 1 round fired from repaired emplacement for purpose of registration; enemy immediately fired several rounds shrapnel and two H.E., the latter appearing short; enemy fired one green flare + his fire ceased. Reserve men used each night as ration party and to carry ammunition. | Locations: Crab Crawl; Mount Sorrel. | Casualties: none.

Corps called with a representation from Army about promotions. | People: Maj. McGillivray. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-31 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Vierstraete Front** — German trench mortars still very inactive, which is so unusual for this front; reconnaissance made to find an emplacement for Stokes gun in support trench at the head of Poppy Lane; good positions found, but communications in daytime were bad. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-31 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Yierstraate sector, Belgium** — Uneventful day; at 10.30 p.m. 'A' and 'C' Sections from company reserve and rest billets respectively relieved 'A' and 'C' Sections in the Yierstraat sector; same indirect fire as on previous nights with same targets; strict gas alert put in force 11 p.m. on Yierstraate–St Eloi sectors; 6th Cdn Inf Bde relieved 4th Cdn Inf Bde on the left. | People: Capt. S. W. Watson. | Companies: 6th Cdn Inf Bde; 4th Cdn Inf Bde. | Casualties: none
- **1916-07-31 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Crab Crawl / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — Day quiet. Work on dug-out continued. General: 43rd Battn. report mortar in Crab Crawl of value to them in silencing enemy rifle grenade fire; also that direct hit was obtained on enemy bombing post and on more than one occasion men in our bombing post heard commotion in enemy trench following our fire — a distinct change of attitude of this battalion toward our trench mortars. 58th Battn. report mortars in Mount Sorrel very useful in silencing enemy T.M. fire, especially as retaliation can be obtained immediately wherever and whenever wanted, which is more difficult with artillery. Stokes mortars especially useful in this sector as lines are so close artillery fire cannot be brought to bear on enemy front line. Signed John E. Ryerson, Capt., O.C. 9th Canadian Trench Mortar Battery. | People: Capt. J. E. Ryerson. | Companies: 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion. | Locations: Crab Crawl; Mount Sorrel. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-31 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Very quiet; indirect fire on enemy tram-lines, roads and dumps carried on; 10 O.R. reported for duty with the company. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1916-08-01 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Mount Sorrel / Crab Crawl, Belgium** — In trenches as on 31 July. Mortars in Mount Sorrel fired 45 rounds on enemy front line and suspected T.M. emplacement; enemy fairly active with his trench mortars. Mortar in Crab Crawl fired 10 rounds in retaliation to rifle grenades on enemy front line. Enemy activity in this portion of front slight. Results of fire seemed good. Casualties nil. | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Crab Crawl. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-08-02 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Crab Crawl / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — 2.30 A.M. 15 rounds fired from Crab Crawl; enemy rifle grenades silenced; a proportion of air bursts obtained apparently with good results. Sorrel enemy fired 7 flares in quick succession from a point [uncertain] and a machine gun [uncertain] in front of his trench about opposite our trench 51 [uncertain]. Fire directed on this point with Stokes — first shot made a direct hit; no more heard from that quarter during the night. Casualties nil. | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Crab Crawl; trench 51. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-08-03 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Mount Sorrel / Crab Crawl / St. Peter St. / Hill 60, Belgium** — 1.30 A.M. one of our patrols encountered an enemy patrol opposite trenches 50/51 and a number of bombs were thrown. Stokes mortars in Mt. Sorrel opened fire on trenches behind where encounter took place, firing 60 rounds; enemy in these trenches [uncertain] threw a large number of bombs into "No Man's Land", doing no damage. Following the blowing of a small mine near Hill 60, mortars in Mt. Sorrel fired 50 rounds on enemy front + support lines. Mortars in Crab Crawl fired 21 rounds and St. Peter St. 19 rounds on enemy front line. Results appeared good; casualties nil. 10.00 P.M. personnel 7th Can. T.M. Bty. arrived at Zillebeke Bund and were given guides to various emplacements. | Companies: 7th Can. T.M. - **1916-08-12 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill 60 / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — 8.30 A.M. enemy opened heavy bombardment on Hill 60 sector + to right of it. 10.00 A.M. enemy infantry attacked. During bombardment and attack, mortars #1 + #2 in this sector fired 129 rounds and #2 37 rounds on enemy front line, creating barrage in "No Man's Land". Corpl. of 60th Can. Battn. states he saw bombs exploding among enemy troops as they advanced across No Man's Land. Dug-outs + emplacements stood the bombardment well. Casualties nil. Mortars in Mount Sorrel joined in retaliatory bombardment, firing #1 35 rounds, #2 25 rounds, #3 25 rounds. Bombing post opposite trench 48 registered on by #3 mortar, 8 rounds being fired. | Companies: 60th Battalion. | Locations: Hill 60; Mount Sorrel; trench 48. | Casualties: none (battery).
- **1916-08-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Promenade, Belgium** — Very heavy artillery and trench mortar bombardment by enemy started 8.15; at 8.30 intense bombardment concentrated on trenches around Railway Cutting; about 9.45 information received Germans are in trench 38; bombing heard but nothing seen owing to intense dust; 10.40 42nd Battn report dense barrage of 5.9 on routes from Valley Cottages; reports trench 46 taken but not confirmed; communication with front line suspended, communication attempted through 52nd Battn at Verbrandenmolen; 6 runners despatched to front line but failed to make connection; 11.35 communication with front battalion established; 60th Battn report trenches much battered, feared casualties heavy; things not serious, situation well in hand; two Lewis guns out of commission but replaced by Colt guns. | Casualties: none (60th Battn casualties feared heavy, unconfirmed). | Movement: —

- **1916-08-14 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill 60 / Railway Dugouts, Belgium** — 3.00 P.M./6.00 P.M. enemy bombarded Hill 60 sector with trench mortars and Minenwerfer (heavy), doing considerable damage. About 5.00 P.M. a direct hit was obtained on Emplacement #2, completely destroying emplacement, mortar, 170 rounds ammunition, and rendering adjoining dug-outs unserviceable. Casualties: **3 killed, 6 wounded and shocked** — 4 men were in dug-outs and door was sealed by earth from explosion; men wounded by flying pieces and by partial collapse of dug-out and affected by gas. Owing to casualties and destruction of ammunition it is unknown what firing was done during the day; 2 of the casualties being from crew of mortar #1, gassed. 7.00 P.M. wired to billet for 2 N.C.O.s + 6 men to replace casualties, arriving at Railway Dug-outs about 10.00 P.M. New mortar set up in Old 60 [uncertain] T.M. emplacement in Allen St., 25 yds in rear of [uncertain] one destroyed. | Locations: Hill 60; Allen St.; Railway Dugouts. | Casualties: **3 killed, 6 wounded and gassed** (battery's heaviest loss of the diary; two of the killed are named in the following entries — Pte. Jeacke and Corpl. A. F. Nelson; the third is not named in the diary).

- **1916-09-07 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Steenvoorde → Bavinchoove → Arques → Auxi-le-Château → Maison Rolland, France** — 2.00 A.M. reveille. 3.00 A.M. breakfast. 4.00 A.M. parade. In preparation for move to new area (9th Brigade Operation Order No. 31). 4.30 A.M. left billet pushing 7 push wagons with mortars, stores, cooking dixies, etc.; 3 mortars and several boxes of stores had to be left behind owing to absolute inadequacy of push wagons as transport — Stokes boxes will not fit in, when loaded very difficult to balance, no drag ropes provided; one G.S. wagon would be far more useful. "Why should men of Light trench mortar batteries do the work that is done in other units by horses and mules?" Tedious march: loads kept slipping, kits fell off, wheels struck stone cobbles and wrenched handles out of men's hands, whole load upset on road. Hills about Cassel especially hard pulling; men soon fatigued even with only about one half the load they would have had if everything had been brought. 9.30 A.M. arrived at Bavinchoove; wagons + loads loaded on motor lorries, men boarded other lorries, 25 men per lorry. 9.15 [uncertain] lorries started, went to railway station at Arques. Arrived at Arques; push wagons loaded on flat cars, men entrained in box cars. 12.49 [uncertain] train moved off. Travelled all day until 1.30 A.M. 8 Sept, when arrived at Aux-I-Le-Chateau. Men detrained, push wagons unloaded. Marched via Maizecourt, Domleger and Cramont to billets in Maison Rolland; march very hard owing to extreme darkness and high hills; on arrival men pushing "push wagons" very fatigued. | Locations: Steenvoorde; Cassel; Bavinchoove; Arques; Aux-I-Le-Chateau; Maizecourt; Domleger; Cramont; Maison Rolland. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Steenvoorde area → Arques by lorry and train → Auxi-le-Château → Maison Rolland (march).

- **1916-09-08 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — 53 patients admitted and 139 evacuated.

- **1916-09-10 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Albert, France** — Church service held at 9 a.m.; R.Cs. paraded to church under Lt Roy; remainder of morning spent cleaning guns, S.A.A. etc.; company left Vadencourt at 2 p.m., passed starting point on Vadencourt–Warloy road at 2 p.m., proceeded by Senlis–Bouzincourt road to Albert and bivouaced in allotted area on the Albert–Bouzincourt road to the north of Albert; no casualties, health very good. | People: Lt. Roy. | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Vadencourt–Albert.
- **1916-09-10 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Maison Rolland → Domart → St. Leger, France** — 10.15 A.M. paraded preparatory to move. Left billet 10.45 A.M., passed starting point Maison Rolland Church at 11.00 A.M. Column delayed on account of very steep hill at Le Plouy, so unit had lunch at Domquer and continued march at 2.30 P.M. via Fransu, Franqueville and Domart, making regular halts of 10 min per hour. At Domart a wrong turning was taken by 9th C.M.G.C., who cut through + passed us on a very steep hill, push carts being too heavy for the men to keep up to marching men or limbers. When top of hill reached, error discovered; necessary to turn about and go down hill again into Domart. When just outside village of Domart, 9th C.M.G.C. made a halt to feed horses. This unit pushed on to St. Leger, arriving at billets in building of the Societe Cooperative La Prevoyance at 6.30 P.M. Men accommodated in open horse sheds, with straw to sleep on. | Companies: 9th C.M.G.C. | Locations: Maison Rolland; Le Plouy; Domquer; Fransu; Franqueville; Domart; St. Leger. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Maison Rolland → St. Leger (march).

Grantham, Bowles and Duthie made a reconnaissance of the area the company was to occupy in Divisional Reserve to the 4th and 6th Bdes during the operations due 15 Sep. | People: Lieut. Duthie; Lieut. - **1916-09-15 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — During the attacks made by 4th and 6th Cdn Inf Bdes the company was held in readiness to move forward at a minute's notice; day passed uneventfully until 5.15 p.m., when it was moved forward to the immediate vicinity of Bde Hdqs, arriving 6.20 p.m.; at 7.30 p.m. B Section under Lieut. Bowles moved forward and succeeded in placing two guns in position in the sunken road just in front of Gun Pit Trench at 9.30 p.m.; Lieut. W. A. Duthie was killed and Lieut. H. B. - **1916-09-16 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Brickfields** — Convoys showed the strain of the long haul, up to 28 miles, and the O.C. had a good look at one of the "land ships" damaged in the previous day's advance. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-09-16 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — At 12.30 a.m. 'D' Section under Lieut. Campbell was sent up to the line with a party of engineers to build and occupy two strong points; Campbell with two guns located along the south side of the Sunken Road 100 yards north-east of the cross roads at R 29 B 6.2, while Sgt. Hobson with the remaining two guns was placed in advanced positions in front of the front line and arrived just in time to assist in repelling the first of a series of five counter-attacks, in all of which these two guns were heavily engaged and assisted materially in repelling; at 9.30 a.m. Lieut. Welch, with two crews of 'A' Section under Sgt. Chamberland, moved off to report to 22nd Bn. Hdqs. in Courcelette; at midnight runners arrived from Lieuts. Bowles and Campbell — Bowles reported a strong enemy counter-attack at 7 p.m. beaten off by his guns assisted by surplus crew acting as riflemen, the enemy coming to a hand-to-hand encounter [uncertain] with the gun crews, and Campbell reported all well; both gun crews suffered casualties from very active enemy snipers and Lieut. Bowles' sergeant was shot and instantly killed early in the day; rations sent up to the gun crews in the line. | People: Lieut. Campbell; Sgt. Hobson; Lieut. Welch; Sgt. Chamberland; Lieut. Bowles. | Companies: 22nd Bn. | Casualties: Lieut. Bowles' sergeant shot and killed; gun crews suffered casualties from enemy snipers.

- **1916-09-17 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — During the night Lieut. Roy was sent in command of 'C' Section to take up positions in Candy Trench between the Bapaume Road and the brigade boundary, guided to its position by Lieut. Grantham, guns placed to command the Bapaume Road and the area in front of Candy Trench; later Roy moved the guns 100 yards further to the right as the area around the Sugar Factory was heavily shelled; at 5 p.m. word received that 1st Cdn. M. G. Coy would relieve the company that night, and at 6 p.m. officers of 6th Cdn. M. G. Coy arrived to arrange the relief; at 7 p.m. Lieut. [uncertain] was sent with two men as guides to take word of the relief to Lieut. Campbell and to locate Sgt. Hobson, the party delayed by heavy shelling and only finding Campbell's position at midnight; two men arrived at Hdqs. with a message from Sgt. Hobson giving his location; Hobson's two gun crews, almost continuously engaged since reaching their position, broke up over five attacks and were in a precarious position as the enemy tried to creep up and bomb them out, one party being put out of action by a shell; his casualties were five. | People: Lieut. - **1916-09-28 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — At 11.20 a.m. word received from senior officer of 'A' and 'D' Sections that the guns were in a very bad place, having come in for heavy shelling owing to the amount of firing done from that location; during the night a direct hit was made on one gun of 'A' Section, gun and tripod destroyed and two men killed and two wounded; at 4 p.m., permission having been obtained through Bde., remaining guns of 'A' and 'D' Sections were withdrawn from strafing positions and placed in company reserve at Hdqs. in Bailiff Wood; at 5 p.m. two guns of 'D' Section under Lieut. Campbell [uncertain] were [uncertain] up to [uncertain] O.C. 26th Bn. and placed at their disposal; at 10 p.m. word received that 'C' Section's area was being heavily shelled, with no further news during the night; during the night 15 of the company transport [uncertain] were sent up by order of the Staff Captain to be used as pack animals. | People: Lieut. Campbell. | Companies: 26th Bn. | Casualties: 2 men killed and 2 wounded when a direct hit destroyed an 'A' Section gun.

'C' Section — during the night his two guns in reserve in the Sunken Road in R 29 a were buried by shells and put out of action, the crews buried with them, [uncertain] four killed, and his sergeant also killed during the night; total casualties to 12 noon: 7 O.R. killed and 5 O.R. wounded and shell shocked; at 3.30 p.m. orders received for two guns from Sugar Trench to report to 25th Bde. - **1916-09-30 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Moulin Neuf / Courcelette, France** — A.M. battery devoted all A.M. to cleaning up clothing + equipment. P.M. ditto under Lieuts. Wells + McCord practised gun drill + laying. 4.00 [uncertain] Lieut. Macdonald reported at B.H.Q., where under Capt. Sills [uncertain] a party representing all units of Bde. went forward to look over line held by 4th + 5th Can. Inf. Bdes., on the right + left respectively, from approx. R 22 c 7 b, 23 a 9 5, 24 c 5 8, M 19 b 0.10, M 20 b 0.3. Arrived H.Q. of 4th + 5th Bdes. 7 A.M. Macdonald went to Courcelette Quarry, where were 4th C.T.M. Bty. They reported no guns in action, as tactical situation + nature of ground + fighting did not permit it. This unit was standing by in case of counter attack by enemy, leaving guns + ammunition with them. Viewed ground from support trench running E from Quarry, in company with Mr. Carey, Lieut. T.M. Bty.; Mr. Gale, Lieut. C.E., 5th T.M. Bty., reported similarly to 4th T.M. Bty. He has half battery + 4 guns at disposal of Bn. commanders at Bn. H.Q.'s. 4th + 5th Bde. H.Q.'s close to each other at about X. 11. C central. Signed R. Macdonald, Lieut., O.C. 9th C.T.M.B. | People: Lieut. R. Macdonald; Capt. - **1916-10-02 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bouzincourt, France** — Information received that Lieut. Campbell had been shell shocked the evening of the 1st, and that one of his guns in the Sunken Road at R 24 C 8.8 (East Mirailmont Road) had been put out of action during the night with two of the crew killed and a third missing; gun and spare parts salvaged during the day and the two men buried; on 5th Cdn. Inf. Brigade being relieved in the night by 6th Cdn Inf Brigade, orders received that the company was under the orders of 6th Cdn Inf Brigade until ordered to withdraw; orders received at 11.35 a.m. and all gun crews notified; at 5 p.m. the company, having all been withdrawn as far as Bailiff Wood and the limbers packed, moved off for Brickfields, Albert, reaching there at 7.30 p.m.; orders then received to move into billets at Bouzincourt for the night, made after the men had had a meal; transport did not move; health very good. | People: Lieut. Campbell. | Companies: 5th Cdn. Inf. Brigade; 6th Cdn Inf Brigade. | Casualties: Lieut. Campbell shell shocked; 2 of his gun crew killed, 1 missing. | Movement: Courcelette–Albert (Brickfields)–Bouzincourt.

- **1916-12-01 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — Anti-aircraft mount and rest erected and placed near the Cross Roads position; laying of trench mats from Cooker Alley through Link Trench to gun emplacement completed; shelter built at this emplacement for ammunition tripod etc.; work carried on a stairway at left section Hqrs., frames made and put into position, five men working ten hours; platform for ammunition box built into the post at the anti-aircraft position; work begun on new M.G. emplacement at M 13 d 4.7, 150 sandbags filled and frames put together; indirect fire by three guns as usual 5.30–9.30 p.m., 4,000 rounds per gun, scarcely any hostile M.G. fire; Capt. Phillips consulted about iron rations, bandoliers and rifles of men returned from 4th Train; reply sent to the A.A. & Q.M.G. against the Y.M.C.A. taking over the running of the canteens; the O.C. refused to parade Capt. Strathy before the G.O.C. without good reason. | People: Capt. Phillips; Capt. Strathy. | Companies: Headquarters Company; 4th Train. | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-20 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — Inter-company relief carried out today, completed at 12 noon; indirect fire on usual targets, 4,000 rounds S.A.A. expended, no enemy retaliation; at Siding M.G. emplacement work progressed favourably, floor completed, revetting done on sides of trench; at the dugout the stairs are now down 24 and 22 steps respectively; at 1.40 p.m. an enemy aeroplane flying low over Bully was engaged by one anti-aircraft gun at Hdqrs., the plane disappearing towards the German lines; a German plane was engaged by one of the guns in the left sector at 2.30 p.m., one belt being fired. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-20 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Our artillery active with light retaliation; in afternoon (3.15 p.m.) 1st Cdn. Bn. attacked enemy lines at A22 b 3345 to A16 c 9600; under cover of barrage by artillery, trench mortars and machine guns they succeeded in entering front line and supports and held them for 1½ hours, when upon a given signal they withdrew; 2 officers and 56 O.R. German prisoners; 1st Cdn. Bn. lost 6 O.R. killed and 18 O.R. wounded, all evacuated; three of our guns took part in barrage work; our casualties: 2 [uncertain] killed and 2 O.R. wounded; firing as usual at night. | Casualties: 2 [uncertain] killed; 2 O.R. wounded (9th M.G. Coy); 1st Cdn. Bn.: 6 O.R. killed, 18 O.R. wounded; 58 German prisoners. | Movement: —

- **1916-12-21 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — Work begun on new latrine at section Hqrs.; 20 yards of trench dug on top of Slag Pile at Fosse 5 to mount a gun on Dec. 25th; at Lemco Alley trench cleaned out, at Bully Alley a rifle rest installed; indirect fire carried out from 11 p.m. to 1 p.m. [as written], a third gun installed at the new indirect-fire position (M 13 d 4.2) firing at target M 21 C 6.3 to M 27 b 7.5, other targets and gun positions as usual, 7,000 rounds expended; training section at Hdqrs. started on two days bombing instruction at the Brigade Bombing Area; enemy artillery and trench mortars quiet. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1916-12-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Bruay** — The rest of Divisional Headquarters moved in today; Bruay's population was 56,000, the Town Major and 49 P.B. men (Imperial) did police duties and sanitary work, water came from deep wells pumped to water towers and distributed through mains, garbage and refuse were thrown on the street, some cases of typhoid were reported among civilians, and Lawson suggested the appointment of a permanent Sanitary Officer for the town. | Casualties: some cases of typhoid reported among civilians (not section personnel).

- **1916-12-25 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — During the morning one gun co-operated with 25th Can Inf Bn raid by using indirect fire 2.45–3.45 a.m., 7,500 rounds fired at usual indirect-fire targets behind enemy's line, enemy retaliated heavily with M.G. only; work at Cross Roads still being carried on; 2,000 rounds indirect fire fired during evening at Cité de Rollencourt, retaliation active; enemy very quiet during day; one gun was in position on top of Slag Pile, Fosse 5, during the whole day but no favourable target offered itself; two sections in reserve and transport section had their Christmas dinner at 1 p.m. | People: — | Companies: 25th Can Inf Bn. | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-25 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Very quiet all day and night; our guns firing as usual. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1917-02-10 | 185th Battalion | Witley** — The 85th Battalion, the only other existing unit of the Nova Scotia Highland Brigade, left at a very early hour this morning for France; a close relationship had ever existed between the two battalions, the 85th having assisted in the 185th's organization, furnished many officers and N.C.O.s, and been in camp with them for about five months; their band, which had gained a good reputation, went with them. This evening a Scotch concert was held in the Men's Mess Room, with songs in the Gaelic tongue enjoyed and understood by no small portion of the audience; the 185th departed from Canada with more Gaelic-speaking men than any other unit of the Canadian Expeditionary Forces. | Companies: 85th Battalion.

- **1917-02-14 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Witley) | Witley Camp, Surrey** — 1 O.R. struck off; waggons detailed by companies. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —

Oliphant reported a satisfactory reason why bradoon bits are used on several of his teams; Lieut. - **1917-03-01 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | La Folie Section, France** — The 4th Canadian Division launched the largest raid yet undertaken by the Canadian Corps on the Western Front, using gas — the first occasion on which Canadian troops had experience of it; the company employed 10 machine guns with the artillery, laying down an effective barrage on the enemy's main communication trenches and expending some 50,000 rounds, with no casualties; gas was discharged at 3 am, machine-gun and artillery fire followed for 40 minutes, and the infantry assaulted about 2 hours 40 minutes after zero hour, conditions normal by about 7.30 am; usual indirect fire that night, 7,500 rds on Petit Vimy and Thelus, and the anti-aircraft gun fired 250 rounds at five German aeroplanes. | People: — | Companies: 4th Canadian Division. | Casualties: none

- **1917-03-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Bruay** — Lines of Headquarters Company at Perfey inspected, nothing to boast about; the O.C. has purposely left the O.C. a free hand for a month to see if he would improve his company; resting points staked out on the Bruay–Divion road; General Sir H. Horne inspected the Transport and was highly pleased, Major Prince Arthur of Connaught present; the transport assembled in order, 3 Engineer technical wagons, 2 Signal, 9th Brigade Transport, 7th Brigade Machine Gun Company, 8th Brigade, 9th Brigade Machine Gun Company, Pioneers, Divisional Train and Field Ambulances, taking up close on 1,000 yards. | People: Gen. Grantham proceeded into the lines and assumed command; the two sections in the line are now disposed — "A" Section Nos. 1, 2, 7, 9 and 8 positions, "B" Section Nos. 10 and 11 and two guns in reserve in Neuville St. Vaast; Nos. 7 and 8 taken over from the 4th Cdn M.G. Coy. on Paynesley Trench and No. 11 position moved to A.3.d.2.5½, the new Section H.Q. there complete; the 50-man brigade working party returned and 32 other ranks, eight from each battalion in the brigade, were attached as carriers; the division now holds the Thelus Section, this brigade the left half from Stafford Street to De la Fourche. | People: Maj. - **1917-03-21 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Thelus Section, France** — Work at No. 2 H.Q. reinforced by extra posts; the sniping gun in action in the morning, dispersing several small parties of Germans on the road near A 5. b. 4½. 5, low visibility in the afternoon; the enemy shelled Neuville St. Vaast intermittently all day with 5.9s and 20 cm H.E., several shells close to Coy H.Q.; trench at No. 7 position knocked in and repaired at night; "B" Section suffered a casualty — 1 other rank killed in Neuville St. Vaast by H.E. while carrying S.A.A. to an indirect-fire position; the attached men of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy were withdrawn; 1,500 rds fired at enemy aeroplanes and 6,000 rds on indirect fire on dumps and battalion H.Q.; two guns kept laid on enemy communication trenches overnight in expectation of a raid; Major Watson returned from map reading course at Pernes. | People: Maj. - **1917-04-09 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Neuville St. Vaast, France** — Under cover of an intense artillery and machine-gun barrage, the Canadian Corps, assisted by the 5th British Division, attacked and took Vimy Ridge, zero hour 5.30 am; company casualties 1 other rank killed and 6 wounded; one tripod of "B" Section put out of action shortly after zero hour but replaced from the Divisional M.G. Repair Centre; by 9.30 am all objectives of the 1st and 5th Brigades had been taken; at 10.30 am "A" Section received orders to move forward and occupy strongpoints Y and Z; at 12.45 pm "C" Section reported all guns in position covering Bonval Ravine; at 1.10 pm orders received for "F" Battery to withdraw; at 3 pm "A" Section reported strongpoints Y and Z reached at 1.20 pm and occupied by a subsection in each, and under Lieut. Creighton's guidance immediately started work to help the engineers complete the strongpoints; Major Watson visited all of "A" & "C" Sections' guns between 12 noon and 3 pm; Lieut. Grantham reconnoitred the forward area 4–8 pm; Capt. J. E. McCorkell reported back at 7.20 pm; "F.S." Battery under Lieut. A. C. Bowles fired 50,000 rounds during the day and was withdrawn in the evening to dugouts for a night's rest. | People: Maj. S. W. Watson; Lieut. Creighton; Lieut. Grantham; Capt. J. E. McCorkell; Lieut. A. C. Bowles. | Companies: 5th British Division; 1st & 5th Bdes. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed, 6 O.R. wounded. | Movement: "A" Section forward to strongpoints Y and Z.
- **1917-04-09 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | La Folie Section** — I, J and K Batteries posted ready for barrage fire in support of 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade's attack on Vimy Ridge; at 5.30 a.m. artillery and machine guns opened intense fire and infantry advanced; barrage moved forward with the attack; in 24 hours after zero the three batteries fired approximately 334,000 rounds; 2 O.R. wounded slightly; two guns of B Section sent to S 22 c under Lieut. Johnson. (O.O. No. 52, undated, attached: I, J and K Battery composition and barrage orders.) | People: Lt. Dickson (8th C.M.G. Coy); Lt. [uncertain] Hale (7th C.M.G. Coy); Lt. Ellis (9th C.M.G. Coy); Lieut. Johnson. | Companies: I Battery; J Battery; K Battery; A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: 2 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —
- **1917-04-09 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Mount St. Eloy, France** — The attack on Vimy began; battery opened fire at 5.30 a.m., engaging S22b 05.60 with Left Section and S22b 45.25; after first round No. 4 gun went out of action owing to lack of pressure in recuperator, and No. 3 gun also went out temporarily for same reason; at plus 17 battery switched to S23a 25.80 (Left) and S16d 70.25 (Right); No. 3 gun soon in action again; at plus 75 switched to S17c 70.70 (Left) and 18a 1.2 (Right); trails digging in quickly; at 3 hrs 19 min guns ordered to switch to A6c 4.4–A2a 3.9; at 301 & plus 416 [uncertain] guns engaged B1d 4½ to 2.4 until about 12.15 p.m., when ordered to engage [uncertain] Trench; all guns now in action; about 2.30 p.m. switched to Banff Trench at S16d 00.20 until 8.50 p.m.; during this last action 2 guns always in action, sometimes four; washers in the recuperators found too thin, causing a leak in the valve; prisoners in batches of 50 and 100 began coming in past the battery at 9.30 a.m.; battle appears almost a complete success, only on the right the 4th Division held up by Hill 145. | Companies: 4th Division. | Locations: Vimy; Banff Trench; Hill 145. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-04-10 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Neuville St. Vaast, France** — Nothing of importance during the night or morning; rations and water got up to all sections; about 11.30 am "C" Section from the head of Bonval Ravine observed a party of 100 enemy between Petit Vimy and Vimy, opened fire and dispersed them with casualties, as was a second party of about 50 fifteen minutes later; the enemy retaliated by shelling the head of the ravine with about 38 77 mms and sweeping it with machine-gun fire; at 3.40 pm word was received that a counter-attack was expected and "F.S." Battery stood to; at 4 pm "F.S." Battery was ordered to prepare to move forward and Capt. McCorkell took over command from Lieut. Bowles, who was ordered to the horse lines being sick; moving forward at 4.30 pm to relieve guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Co. in "F.1" position, Capt. McCorkell found these guns were not at that location, so he moved the battery to the correct location at 5.35 pm; command of the battery passed from Major Watson to Major Basevi, O.C. 14th Can. M.G. Co.; the order was changed at 6.40 pm, command of "D.1", "E.1" and "F.1" batteries passing to Major Watson, who was ordered to have them take up entirely new positions further forward; casualties total for the two days now 1 other rank killed and 7 wounded. | People: Capt. J. E. McCorkell; Lieut. Bowles; Maj. Basevi; Maj. S. W. Watson. | Companies: 14th Cdn. M.G. Co. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed, 7 O.R. wounded (two-day total).

- **1917-04-13 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy Ridge, France** — Lieut. McBurny took over command of "F.1" Battery from Capt. McCorkell, who returned to the transport lines; Lieut. Robson reported to Lieut. McBurny and is in charge of "B" Section; the battery is again under control of Major S. W. Watson; the 5th Bde. relieved the 4th Bde. in the afternoon, taking over Bde. H.Q. in the cave at Les Tilleuls, Major Watson moving to this point with the brigade; during the afternoon and evening the line was advanced over the railroad embankment, the town of Vimy having been taken; a reconnaissance was made in the evening by Major Watson and Lieut. Creighton in advance of the railway embankment where the 18th Bn. were found digging in; "A" & "C" sections moved forward and took up positions on the railway embankment, "B" & "D" sections held in reserve at the head of Bonval Ravine; sixteen of the attached Bde. carriers were returned at night; casualties 1 other rank killed and 3 wounded, two of which were caused by a bomb explosion in the bottom of a trench. | People: Lieut. Creighton. | Companies: 5th Bde.; 4th Bde.; 18th Bn. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed, 3 O.R. wounded (2 by bomb explosion in a trench). | Movement: "A" & "C" sections forward to the railway embankment.

Line, France** — At 5.40 am "D" Section was ordered to move forward and take up protective positions covering the brigade front on a line in advance of Mount Forêt quarries; by 6.30 am the company was disposed — "D" Section 4 guns between T15b 9.2 and T16 D 3.3 with H.Q. in Mount Forêt quarries, "A" Section 4 guns along the railway embankment, "C" Section 4 guns in line along the R.R. embankment, "B" Section still in reserve at the head of Bonval Ravine; company advanced H.Q. established in a German dugout at T26 B 9.4; a base established at the head of Bonval Ravine; rations delayed so late, owing to the transport lines moving to Aux Rietz and the ration dumps being moved, that it was impossible to get them up owing to darkness; a draft of 10 other ranks received. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: "D" Section forward to Mount Forêt quarries; advanced H.Q. to T26 B 9.4.

- **1917-04-28 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy–Farbus R.R. Embt., France** — During the night of 27/28th the 26th Cdn. Inf. Bn. dug in in T23b, 600 yds in advance of their old line; 2 guns of "B" Section were placed at T23 d 5.9½ to protect the right flank of the 26th Bn. and the brigade front; at 4.25 am the Canadian Corps attacked Arleux-en-Gohelle in conjunction with operations by the 3rd Army further south; Nos. 4, 5, 6 and 7 M.G. Batteries under Major S. W. Watson formed a supporting and protective barrage with the artillery, and the 25th Cdn. Inf. Bn. advanced to connect with the 26th Bn.; the operation was successful and all objectives were reported taken; 162,000 rds S.A.A. expended by the four batteries 4.25–6.55 am; a gun and crew of "B" Section at T23 d 5.9½ was buried by the German counter-barrage at 4.30 am, 2 other ranks killed and 1 wounded, the remainder — Cpl. Ronayne and 1 other rank — dug out unhurt three hours later by Pte. Brown, the gun slightly damaged but not put out of action; at 8.30 pm the enemy put up an S.O.S. on the right flank and all batteries opened fire, 17,000 rds; one gun of the Borden Battery was put out of action by shrapnel but replaced immediately from the Div. Repair Centre; casualties among attached units 1 other rank killed and 2 wounded. | People: Maj. S. W. Watson; Cpl. Ronayne; Pte. Brown. | Companies: 26th Cdn. Inf. Bn.; 25th Cdn. Inf. Bn.; Borden Battery. | Casualties: 2 O.R. killed, 1 O.R. wounded (company); attached units 1 O.R. killed, 2 O.R. wounded.
- **1917-04-28 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — A and B Sections at T 16 d and C and D Sections at T 16 d put a barrage on the enemy line from T 11 a to T 18 b; zero 4.25 a.m., firing continued until zero + 150; objective gained and consolidated; company returned to M.G. Fort except A Section, which relieved D Section in North Vimy defences. | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: → M.G. Fort.

- **1917-04-30 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy–Farbus R.R. Embt., France** — In answer to an S.O.S. at 4.30 am all machine-gun batteries opened fire on their protective barrage for a short time, 25,000 rds; the remainder of the day passed quietly with the usual shelling of the forward area; orders received in the afternoon for Nos. 5 and 6 Batteries (14th Cdn. M.G. Co.) to be withdrawn in the evening to rest, and later word that No. 4 Battery (1st Cdn. M.M.G.) would also be withdrawn, so No. 7 Battery was dissolved and "C" Section was ordered to man positions in the sunken road at T28a 5.5 for indirect fire on the enemy's trenches and wire, and "D" Section to carry out indirect fire on the streets and crossroads in Acheville; the enemy maintained an intensive bombardment on Mt. Forêt Quarries and the forward area from 5.30 pm, evidently suspecting the relief of the 25th Bn. by the 24th Bn. (Signed Maj. S. W. Watson.) | People: Maj. S. W. Watson. | Companies: 14th Cdn. M.G. Co.; 1st Cdn. M.M.G.; 25th Bn.; 24th Bn. | Casualties: none

Appendix 3: Gouy Yard plan. Appendix 4 (order 1.5.17) not located in this volume. | Company: A Coy; 1st East Surrey Regiment (attached).

- **1917-05-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright, considerable aeroplane activity; inspected the area in advance of Divisional Headquarters, the Nine Elms area and the heavy shelling of Bois Carré and Thélus, finding a great deal of old refuse about, especially round the old German front line position, and the dead body of a German not yet buried, which was reported to the A.A. & Q.M.G. with a fatigue party of 50 men asked for, then in the afternoon inspected the Fond de Vase area and the 3rd Brigade transport lines, reported as unsatisfactory, with conditions very bad in respect to latrines and refuse holes, reported to the A.D.M.S., and the lorry was moved from Ecoivres to Ariane dump. | Casualties: none.

Beasley; Capt. Hennessy; Lt. Grant. | Companies: — | Casualties: none (shelling, no casualties)

- **1917-05-02 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — During the night of 1st/2nd the usual indirect fire was carried out on the usual targets, 24,000 rounds; the enemy retaliated with H.E. and gas shell, doing no damage; the enemy heavily shelled the R.R. Embankment and vicinity of Coy H.Q. between midnight and 2 am with H.E., causing 1 casualty at Coy H.Q.; the 6th Cdn. Inf. Bde. relieved the 24th Bn. in the right half of the divisional sector during the night of 2nd/3rd; Major Watson issued Preliminary Order M.G. 461, and as Coy H.Q. was required for a 6th Bde. battalion H.Q., a new H.Q. was established in the R.R. Embankment at T26.A.6.2; in addition to the company's 8 mobile guns, 2 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. and 6 guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. on the Farbus–Vimy R.R. Embankment and 6 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Co. in the observation line on Vimy Ridge were detached to the 5th Bde.; at 7.30 pm Major Watson received orders to assume command of the barrage guns of the division, Major Eastham having been evacuated sick, and immediately issued the instructions in M.G. 469 and established his H.Q. with the O.C. 6th Bde. in Thelus Mill Cave. | People: Maj. S. W. Watson; Maj. Eastham. | Companies: 6th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 24th Bn.; 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 1 casualty at Coy H.Q.
- **1917-05-02 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Hostile artillery quieter from 7 a.m. but much air activity; enemy shelled the whole area intermittently, Vimy Station, railway embankment, Chaudiere and Andros Corner receiving special attention; our artillery put on a practice barrage at 5.25 a.m.; enemy machine guns active sweeping roads and approaches to the front line at night. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1917-05-02 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright, warm; inspected the area patrolled by Sgt. Williams forward of the Lens–Arras road in the morning, the trenches east of Nine Elms, at present occupied by the 13th Battalion, exceedingly dirty though cleaned up two days ago by a fatigue party obtained by this unit, the battalions occupying them having paid no attention to sanitary orders issued, reported to the A.A. & Q.M.G., and the bodies of two Germans were found and the Camp Commandant of the area notified, the artillery position on the slope of the hill in fairly good shape and the 13th Machine Gun Company lines very dirty, with Thélus and Bois Carré heavily shelled, then in the afternoon rode through the Bunechaut Camp area, where some improvement had been made following the adverse report sent in yesterday, and sent a report to the A.D.M.S. regarding the condition of latrines in the 1st Canadian Divisional area. | People: Sgt. Williams. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — Indirect fire midnight to dawn on the streets and crossroads in Acheville and the enemy's support line wire, 10,000 rds; at 3.45 am the 6th Bde., in conjunction with operations of the 1st Cdn. Div. and XIII Corps on the right, attacked the German trench system south of Acheville, the attack not entirely successful, being partly held up by machine guns in a reinforced concrete emplacement on the high ground at U19.C.0.4; the 5th Bde. did not take part, but held the ground already occupied; two of the company's sections, "C" & "D", were employed on barrage work and known as 7 Battery; a counter-attack expected at 8.15 am came to naught on the guns opening up; the transport pack train delivered 30,000 rds to No. 7 Battery; one gun of "C" Section was put out of action at 9.30 pm by a shell bursting close to the emplacement, the No. 1, Pte. D. W. Graham, killed and 2 other ranks wounded, one of whom died at a Casualty Clearing Station. | People: Pte. D. W. Graham. | Companies: 6th Bde.; 1st Cdn. Div.; XIII Corps. | Casualties: Pte. D. W. Graham killed; 2 O.R. wounded, one died at C.C.S.

- **1917-05-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Ecurie, France** — Routine day. Admitted 7 horses. | People: No. 484 Pte. Reidy J. P., rejoined from 1 Canadian Divisional Train | Casualties: none.
- **1917-05-03 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright; left at 5.30 a.m. with Col. R. [uncertain] Simpson, C.A.M.C., and Col. Templeton, D.A.D.M.S., for the advanced dressing stations and regimental aid posts, the wounded beginning to come in fairly early and many walking cases met on the way up, returning about 9 a.m. to report to Col. Ford, A.D.M.S., that the wounded were being brought out from the front line satisfactorily, then assisted at the main dressing station, with Col. Ross and Captain Gibson, Canadian Corps, visiting the office, the wounded practically all cleared before 1 p.m., and in the afternoon called on the Camp Commandant of the forward area to arrange for the burial of some dead Germans, with the Sanitary Section lorry loaned to the A.D.M.S. for transport of walking wounded from the hospital at Carency [uncertain] to Barlin. | People: Col. R. [uncertain] Simpson; Col. Templeton; Col. Ford; Col. Ross; Capt. Gibson. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-04 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Gaumont, France** — Battery detailed for two aerial shoots; one commencing 4.10 p.m. a failure owing to airman being short of petrol — he observed only three rounds then returned; second shoot did not materialize; battery fired 250 rounds on special targets, and retaliation during the night; battery shelled intermittently during the night; no material damage and no casualties. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-05-04 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Ecurie, France** — Weekly reports rendered to A.D.V.S. and A.A. + Q.M.G.; 20 other ranks (No. 13 Veterinary Hospital) rejoined this unit from No. 3 M.V.S. Admitted 17 horses. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-05-04 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright, very warm and hazy; rode to the Fond de Vase area in the morning and inspected the lines at Bunechaut Farm, the 3rd Brigade Trench Mortar Battery lines in filthy condition, interviewed Captain Tennant, Camp Commandant of this area, and seven shells were sent into Bunechaut Farm this morning, then in the afternoon drove to Camblain l'Abbé, called on the D.D.M.S. Canadian Corps and discussed sanitation during the warm season, suggesting that a separate report be made by the Sanitary Officer on each unit, marking them excellent, good or unsatisfactory, these reports to be published in Divisional Orders, with Major Rankin, Canadian Corps, and Captain McDonald, O.C. 3rd Canadian Sanitary Section, present at the discussion. | People: Capt. Tennant; Major Rankin; Capt. McDonald. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-05 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Gaumont, France** — Battery engaged several hostile batteries during the day; one aeroplane shoot carried out, 150 rounds fired, result satisfactory; at 3 a.m. 2 batteries engaged in answer to S.O.S. call from infantry; light shelling throughout the 24 hours by 5.9 enemy batteries; no casualties. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, warm; the 1st Canadian Brigade was relieved last night by troops of the 5th Division, the lorry reported at 8 a.m. to move the office supplies of the A.D.M.S. to Bruay, Lt-Col. Scott, 14th Field Ambulance, called and arranged to hold the dugouts used for the A.D.M.S. office and personnel for future medical units, the A.D.M.S. 5th Division later concurring, Staff Sgt. Kitteringham was instructed to move the men into these dugouts, and at Divisional Headquarters Major Wake, D.A.A.G., said the area had been cleaned up and would be left in a sanitary condition by the Division, then in the afternoon drove to Bunechaut Farm, where the lines vacated by the various transports were in a very unsatisfactory condition, the 5th Division not yet having put in a Camp Commandant for the Fond de Vase area, and called to investigate a nuisance complained of in the 2nd Anti-Aircraft Battery, the conditions already remedied, and later called on the D.D.M.S. 13th Corps to arrange for all 13th Corps orders on sanitation to be forwarded, with Pte. Beckerson returned from hospital, very quiet with little artillery fire and few aeroplanes observed. | People: Lt-Col. Scott; Staff Sgt. Kitteringham; Major Wake; Pte. Beckerson. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-07 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | La Targette** — Supply train late again and had to turn back after nearly reaching the railhead, immediately after Traffic wired complaining of delay in unloading; last night a German aeroplane came over these lines 150 yards N.N.W. of La Targette after all our planes had gone home by 8.30 p.m. and tried to set fire to one of our balloons, missing three times with his flares and firing his machine gun on the ground with no damage as far as can be ascertained; the same thing happened on the night of the 3rd, when the plane dropped bombs and did damage, killing two men, wounding several others and killing three horses. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 killed, several wounded, 3 horses killed (German bombing, night of 3 May; the men are not named)

- **1917-05-07 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — During the past night the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. relieved the 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. in the forward area, the 5th Bde. proceeding to rest camp at Aux Reitz, the company remaining in the line for another 24 hours to cover the relief; the day passed quietly with only the normal amount of shelling up to 10 pm, when the enemy opened a heavy bombardment with gas shells on the whole divisional front from the tops of Vimy Ridge to forward of the Vimy–Farbus R.R. Embankment; No. 7 Battery ("C" & "D" sections) were withdrawn at dusk and proceeded to rest camp at Aux Reitz, fortunately only one casualty during this withdrawal although several men were slightly gassed; arrangements completed and guides provided for the relief of "A" & "B" Sections by one section of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. and one section of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | People: — | Companies: 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 4th Cdn. M.G. - **1917-05-08 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — During the night of 7th/8th "A" & "B" sections were relieved by one section each of the 4th and 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy., the relief hampered by gas shelling which continued the whole night until 5 am; on completion of the relief at 2 am, "A" & "B" sections proceeded to Aux Reitz, the last section arriving at 8 am; both sections were clear of the forward area before the enemy's dawn counter-attack, in which he recaptured Fresnoy from the 5th British Div. and the portion of the Oppy–Mericourt line held by this division; the remainder of the day was spent resting, the men fatigued, several suffering from the effects of the gas shells; the company bathed at Neuville-St. Vaast; two guns were mounted at dawn for A.A. work at Divisional H.Q., Aux Reitz, and another at the camp. | People: — | Companies: 4th & 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 5th British Div. | Casualties: several men suffering gas effects. | Movement: "A" & "B" sections to Aux Reitz.

Division inspected the Train in the afternoon, spending two hours at it, and presented Meritorious Medals to S.S.M. Proctor and S.S. Wade; the R.C.R. kindly lent their fife band for the march past; the G.O.C. expressed much satisfaction. | People: S.S.M. Proctor; S.S. Wade. | Companies: R.C.R. | Casualties: none
- **1917-05-14 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Witley) | Witley Camp, Surrey** — 4 officers and 4 N.C.O.s start anti-gas course. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —
- **1917-05-14 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy Station, France** — The relief completed by 2 am; "C" Section guns in the front line and "D" Section 3 guns at T22 A 9.7 and 1 gun at T29 A 3.0, "A" & "B" sections coming back under orders of the G.O.C. 5th Bde.; 8 guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. in strong points and 9 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Co. on barrage work at T29 A 3.0 also came under the G.O.C. 5th Bde.; in the morning at about 10 o'clock one gun of "D" Section was put out of action, 2 of the gun crew killed and an attached carrier wounded by shell fire; at 1 pm the enemy commenced shelling the R.R. Embankment from Vimy Station to about 600 yds south, mostly 5.9s, until about 5 pm, one entrance to Advance H.Q. blown in but no casualties; at dusk two sections of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy. relieved "A" & "B" sections in positions 300 yds in advance of the R.R. Embankment (O.O. No. 5); further orders — "B" Section only relieved the two sections of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. at T29 A 3.0 forming a protective barrage on the German front line, and "A" Section moved to the old battery position at T16 B 6.0; moves completed and guns in position by 11.15 pm; each section has guns detailed for A.A. work; casualties 2 other ranks killed, 1 died of wounds, 1 wounded, all "D" Section. | People: — | Companies: 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 4th Cdn. M.G. Co.; 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 2 O.R. killed, 1 O.R. died of wounds, 1 O.R. wounded ("D" Section).
- **1917-05-14 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Enemy artillery fairly active, many shells at Vimy Station and Vimy (mostly 4.2s) and at the railway embankment; enemy planes fairly active, one over the Quarries driven back by machine-gun fire. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1917-05-14 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Gaumont, France** — Battery heavily shelled with gas and H.E., no effect; 160 rounds fired on neutralization of hostile batteries with good results; Nos. 2, 3 and 4 guns out of action. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-14 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Dull, rain in the afternoon; inspected the area around the old Divisional Headquarters at Arras in the morning, the A.D.M.S. 5th Division and part of the 5th Divisional Headquarters who were located there having moved to Roclincourt, then in the afternoon a telegram from the A.D.M.S. 1st Canadian Division asking for a report at Bruay, proceeding by lorry via Souchez and Carency with Captain O'Hagan, M.O. 1st Canadian Divisional Train, to a meeting of medical officers at which many points of interest were discussed. | People: Capt. O'Hagan. | Casualties: none.

A Coy preparing to lay track east of Thelus; this part of line badly shelled. C Coy organised into 13 parties for maintenance. D Coy divided into three parts, each working 8 hours through the 24-hour day on account of shelling, to obtain the part of the day when no shelling was going on. Labour attached: D Coy 4 officers, 383 OR, 19th (Queen's) RWS, and 2 officers, 316 OR, 4th Devons; C Coy 4 officers, 263 OR, DCLI Pioneers; A Coy 3 officers, 411 OR, 27th Labour Coy. Webb called in the evening with the result of the competition; the G.O.C. referred the case of a Salvage Lance Corporal to the O.C., who dealt with him by reverting him to the ranks; Section 2 of 4th Reserve Park inspected at Barlin, horses much improved; "Louise" came in three times, splattering mud but no damage; Driver Flannigan of A.F.A. Brigade tried for neglecting to obey an order, 14 days F.P. No. 1; Private Willis, loader from No. 3 Coy, dismissed for filthy language to the S.M. and ordered back to his unit. | People: Col. - **1917-06-01 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy Station, France** — The day was exceptionally quiet; work done deepening trenches and on latrines at gun positions; the 5th Bde. was relieved by the 3rd Cdn. Inf. Bde. during the evening, but the company remained in the line another day; officers and other ranks of the 2nd Cdn. M.G. Coy. arrived in the trenches with rations to spend a day at gun positions before taking over the line. | People: — | Companies: 5th Bde.; 3rd Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 2nd Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: none
- **1917-06-01 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Night comparatively calm; Lt. Soulsby was killed last night (31 May/1 June) at the entrance of his dugout; day quiet round most of the line with usual intermittent shelling of the Culvert and gun pits; aircraft very active — three enemy planes over our positions at 10 a.m. turned back by machine-gun fire, and at 10.45 a.m. four enemy planes attacked one of our scout planes west of the railway embankment and brought it down in flames just behind our front line, both airmen burned to death; enemy shelled front line east of the railway embankment and the Culvert in the afternoon; eight enemy planes over our positions at 8.45 p.m. | People: Lt. Soulsby. | Casualties: Lt. Soulsby killed (night 31 May/1 June); 2 airmen burned to death. | Movement: —

- **1917-06-01 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Gaumont, France** — Wire-cutting tasks throughout the day, 106 E fuse being used; results reported very good; very quiet in vicinity of battery position; in the night harassing fire on cross roads maintained. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-06-02 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Night 1st/2nd fairly quiet; at 2.55 a.m. enemy sent up red flares in pairs, machine guns opened up and front line shelled until 3 a.m.; 3,000 rounds fired on targets engaged by artillery during the day; enemy heavily shelled a battery at T 13 c with 5.9" guns 3–3.45 p.m., over 100 heavy shells, apparently one direct hit; enemy aircraft not very active. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-06-02 | 9th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Alberta) | Bramshott, England** — Pte. W. H. Brooks S.O.S. on appointment to a commission in the Imperial Army. Net decrease 20 Other Ranks; net decrease 4 Other Ranks. | People: Pte. W. H. Brooks. | Casualties: none.

Bn. sent out patrols and found Avion Trench west of the railway strongly manned, and it was reported, though not confirmed, that Avion Trench from the railway to Victoria Road is occupied by the 43rd; about 20 prisoners taken up to this evening; dugouts fairly numerous and in good condition; during the evening patrols from the 43rd, 52nd and 58th entered Avion; one of our sergeants and one O.R. wounded; about 7 a.m. we attacked along the whole front, very successfully. | Casualties: 1 sergeant and 1 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —

C.R.T. regarding the provision of rifles for the personnel of this unit; replied that the present issue of 25 rifles per company be increased to 50 rifles per company for use of men in most forward part of light railways and against aeroplanes — a full issue would be considered an encumbrance and a hindrance to the work. One officer admitted to F.A. suffering from gastritis. The attached labour required by this unit in future is shown on Appendix I, which does not include Lestrem work. | Appendix I: Distribution of skilled and unskilled labour for maintenance, First Army — A Coy 212 skilled (Major Barber), territory Laurel Loop to Vimy via Portsmouth, Territorial, Thelus–Ecurie; B Coy 212 skilled (Major Stewart), territory Barlin–Savy, Hersin–Aix Noulette, Ablain Branch, Carency Branch; C Coy 160 skilled (Major Mackenzie), territory Camblain Jc. to St. Catherines via Maroeuil & Artillery Corner; D Coy 212 skilled (Major Duff), territory Roclincourt Jc.–Arleux Bailleul, Gavrelle, Roclincourt Branch; Artillery Corner (Lt. Advised B Coy that they were to take over maintenance of line from Barlin to Verdrel on Monday 23rd inst. from A Coy and turn over portion of line from Camblain to Ecoivres to C Coy. | Appendix II: letter E-3-1627 (1 August 1917) from O.C. to O i/c 3rd Div. It is intended eventually to move the whole of C Coy to Lestrem area, the maintenance now being done by C Coy being taken over by D and A Coys. 1 officer and 21 OR took over dugouts in Thelus village belonging to Canadian Corps Tramways and got things in readiness for maintaining their lines. | Companies: A Coy; B Coy; C Coy; D Coy.

Having received query from H.Q. C.R.T. regarding the employment of French civilian labour, replied as shown in appendix. Twenty cars on light railway system are now being allotted for construction purposes only. Chief Engineer of this unit returned from Audruicq having proceeded [uncertain] connected with [uncertain]. | Appendix III: Minute II (W-1-1413, 22 July 1917) re civilian labour — daily averages employed on railway grading (earthworks): A & B Coys: 8–9 June 130, 11–16 June 130, 18–23 June 99, 25–30 June 72, 2–7 July 79, 9–14 July 102, 16–21 July 113; C Coy does not anticipate employing further civilian labour; D Coy authority C.E. 11th Corps; civilian labour not employed on Sundays. | Companies: A Coy.
