- **1917-08-15 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Lens Sector** — Operations as per Operation Order No. 18 a complete success; zero hour 4.25 am and all guns went over as directed and arrived at their objective, with the exception of No. 3 Gun of "D" Section, knocked out by a direct hit by a shell; a new gun was procured from Ordnance and a new team made up and the gun put in position before nightfall; reports in the O.C.'s hands at 10 am from Lieut. Much, O.C. "C" Section, and Lieut. Creighton, O.C. "D" Section; 3 O.R. killed and 7 O.R. wounded; enemy tried desperately to retake the ground with heavy counter-attacks every few minutes but to no avail; "A" & "B" Sections under Lieut. [uncertain] and Lieut. MacLaren carried on with the barrage as laid down in barrage instructions, expending 75,000 rds S.A.A., under Major Bassevi, O.C. 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy., Group Commander. | People: Lieut. Much; Lieut. Creighton; Lieut. [uncertain]; Lieut. MacLaren; Major Bassevi. | Companies: "C"/"D" Sections; "A"/"B" Sections; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 3 O.R. killed; 7 O.R. wounded; No. 3 Gun, "D" Section knocked out by a direct shell hit.
- **1917-08-15 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Burbure → Villers au Bois** — Company moved from Burbure to Villers au Bois. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Burbure → Villers au Bois.
- **1917-08-15 | 9th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Alberta) | Bramshott, England** — Net increase 3 Other Ranks. Sir Francis Howard and staff, Brig. Gen. [uncertain] and staff, and Brig. General [uncertain] and staff visited the battalion and inspected the training of the men in the various branches. | People: Sir Francis Howard. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-08-15 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Caumont, France** — Barrage fire on enemy positions maintained 5–10 a.m., about 460 rounds fired; at 8 a.m. enemy heavily shelled our rear position, No. 1 gun put out of action, and we had 4 casualties: Gnr. Fairfowl killed, Bdr. Horwill [written "Norwill" on the casualty page], Gnr. Altham and Gnr. Mitchell W.H. severely wounded; C.O. desires to place on record the coolness and devotion to duty shown by the officer, NCOs and men of this section at a time when it was essential that fire should be maintained; names of Lieut. Hoare, Cpl. Troop and Bdr. Horwill submitted to H.Q. for consideration of award in connection with the above action. | People: Gnr Fairfowl; Bdr. Horwill [written "Norwill" on the casualty page]; Gnr Altham; Gnr Mitchell W.H.; Lieut. Hoare; Cpl. Troop. | Casualties: Gnr Fairfowl killed; Bdr. Horwill, Gnr Altham, Gnr Mitchell W.H. severely wounded.

- **1917-09-04 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bouvigny → Vimy (Aux Ritz)** — Company paraded at 7 a.m. and moved to new Transport Lines near Aux Ritz Corner (A 8 c), arriving at 12 noon; rest of day spent preparing for the trenches; on night 4th/5th the 9th Can. M.G. Coy relieved the 92nd Machine Gun Company (Imperial unit): A Section and B Section guns at Aintree, Ascot, Auk and Buffalo; B Section in reserve at Condor; C Section at Badger and Bulldog; D Section in reserve at Coyote and Cobra; one B Section gun at Antelope under command of 15th Can. M.G. Coy; relief completed by 12 midnight; between 12 and 1 a.m. enemy fired a considerable number of gas shells, causing quite a few casualties among the infantry during a relief, and 2 O.R. of ours wounded gassed; gas shells had a mustard odour; strength going into the line 10 officers, 178 O.R. and 44 attached O.R. (O.O. No. 74, dated 4 Sep 1917, attached.) | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: 2 O.R. wounded gassed. | Movement: Bouvigny → Aux Ritz; → Vimy line.

- **1917-09-06 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Caumont, France** — At about 1 a.m. enemy carried out an unprecedented bombardment of this village — gas shell, H.E. and shrapnel fired into all parts of the village, undoubtedly the heaviest bombardment yet experienced by this battery; lasted till 3.45 a.m.; considered at least 5,000 gas shells fired, some of very large calibre; owing to effective precautions taken, casualties small — only 3 men gassed: Grs. Brunton and Thorne, and 1st A.M. Lee of the R.F.C.; at about 7 a.m. an enemy shell burst on roadway near battery position, and Gr. E. F. Martin was killed; two S.O.S. calls responded to and fire put on to Lens area at 7.35 and 8.20 p.m. | People: Gnr Brunton; Gnr Thorne; 1st A.M. Lee (R.F.C.); Gnr E. F. Martin. | Companies: R.F.C. | Locations: Lens. | Casualties: Gnr E. F. Martin killed; Gnr Brunton, Gnr Thorne and 1st A.M. Lee (R.F.C.) gassed.

- **1917-09-07 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Day very quiet; at 5.30 p.m. enemy shelled our anti-aircraft battery (13 pr.) in S 18 c, then shortened range into T 17 d and T 13 a; at 9 and 9.30 p.m. about 15 H.E. shells between S 24 a and S 32 a; during the night 9.30–11 p.m. reliefs carried out: four guns of B Section relieved four guns of No. 4 Section 10th Can. - **1917-10-08 to 1917-10-18 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Caumont, France** — Major S. A. Heward proceeded on leave to England and Captain H. R. N. Cobbett took over temporary command; owing to removal of greater part of artillery from this sector, and apparent scarcity of ammunition, operations practically ceased; during this period battery did not fire more than an average of 50 rounds per diem, chiefly harassing fire; at about 11.30 p.m. on 17th, word received to move to Belgium, and at hour [uncertain] stores and kit were loaded on lorries in a heavy rain storm; battery paraded at 12.30 p.m., leaving behind a rear party of 1 officer (Lieut. E. S. Hoare) and 10 other ranks; proceeded to rendezvous at Hersin, where met by ammunition column; whole column proceeded by road through Noeux-le-Mines and Bethune to Hazebrouck, arriving about 4.15 p.m. | People: Maj. S. A. Heward; Capt. H. R. N. Cobbett; Lieut. E. S. Hoare. | Locations: Hersin; Noeux-le-Mines; Bethune; Hazebrouck. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Cité de Caumont–Hersin–Hazebrouck; rear party left behind.

- **1917-10-26 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Passchendaele** — Attack launched at 5.40 a.m. by 8th and 9th Can. Inf. Brigades on the Passchendaele outer defences, including Bellevue Spur; guns jumped off with the infantry as pre-arranged. On the 4th C.M.R. frontage Lieut. Searles and two guns took up positions at D 4 b, consolidating after the infantry retired and left them isolated; Searles went back, reorganised the infantry and led them forward to consolidate the crest; eight machine guns were taken from pill-boxes at D 4 b but could not be brought out. Sniping battery D 4 a: four guns under Lieut. Duthie reached D 4 a and came into action; when the infantry retired the guns were withdrawn after losing 1 officer and 2 gun crews, then two guns advanced again under Sgt. Love to defensive positions at D 4 a, later moving back to D 4 a. On the 43rd Bn. frontage Lieut. Ellis M.C. was wounded in the shoulder but carried on, getting two guns into action at D 4 d at 6 a.m.; two guns were knocked out before reaching position; Ellis was evacuated at 9 a.m., leaving guns to Pte. Scott C.H. and Pte. Gallant E. At 10 a.m. a party of enemy estimated at two companies was engaged on the Mosselmarkt–Gravenstaple Road with heavy casualties inflicted; at 4 p.m. guns engaged enemy coming up to counter-attack positions, and at the attack on the Camouflage pill-boxes guns neutralised enemy machine-gun fire and engaged escaping enemy, several surrendering. On the 58th Bn. frontage two guns under Lieut. Madgett jumped off at zero, waited about 100 yards, then on the retirement of the infantry made a stand under heavy fire until the 58th Bn. advanced over them, when they withdrew as the gun was out of action. Sniping guns D 16 b opened fire on Meetcheele and Grafh Wood until +120, firing again on 27th. Casualties: officers wounded Capt. E. I. H. Ings, Lt. M. L. Ellis, Lt. J. H. Duthie; 8 O.R. killed, 30 O.R. wounded; reinforcements 10 O.R. | People: Lieut. Searles; Lieut. Duthie; Sgt. Love; Lieut. Ellis M.C.; Pte. Scott C.H. 252201; Pte. Gallant E. 437170; Lieut. Madgett; Capt. E. I. H. Ings; Lt. M. L. Ellis; Lt. J. H. Duthie. | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: Capt. E. I. H. Ings, Lt. M. L. Ellis and Lt. J. H. Duthie wounded; 8 O.R. killed; 30 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —

Smith and Gunner L. C. Aston were severely wounded while keeping telephone communications in repair; billets again attacked by enemy airmen, but no damage done. | People: A/Cpl J. Smith; Gnr L. C. Aston. | Locations: Passchendaele Church; Hamburg O.P. | Casualties: A/Cpl J. Smith and Gnr L. C. Aston severely wounded.

- **1917-10-30 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 5.55 a.m. opened up on line barrage in support of further attack by 3rd and 4th Canadian Divisions; at 8.30 a.m. protective barrage fired and continued till 11.30 a.m.; No. 1 + 3 guns go out of action; S.O.S. lines re-adjusted to roads leading from Passchendaele Church, N and E, but at 1.15 p.m. firing on original protective barrage lines; attack reported very successful; Crest Farm, one of our targets, reported demolished; recommendation for M.C. forwarded to H.Q. for an officer of battery for conspicuous gallantry and devotion to duty, and recommendations for M.M. forwarded for one N.C.O. and one man, in connection with duty at Hamburg O.P. on 27th; advance party of new section (No. 3) arrived — Lieut. No. 53 the company moved from Labrearde to the Potijze area, the transport under Lt. Creighton moving off at 6.30 a.m. and arriving at 4 p.m., while the company, less transport, entrained at Caestre at 12.45 p.m. and proceeded via Godewaersvelde and Poperinghe to the Asylum at Ypres, detraining and marching through Ypres to lines at 1.3.d.1.4 at 3.15 p.m., taking over the lines of the 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; at 5 p.m. "D" Section (1 sergeant, 1 corporal and 24 men) under Lt. H. A. McBurney moved off for the line and relieved four barrage guns of the 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy. under Lieut. Coys also on the same train as well as the Princess Pats, 49th and 52nd Bns.; train left about 11 a.m. and arrived at Abeele at 11.45 a.m.; company marched to a farm at K 24 b, about halfway between Abeele and Watou, where billets had been arranged by Lieut. Rayner; company housed in tents except B and C Sections in a barn; transport arrived about 2 p.m. at Trappiste Corner and all was settled in the new camp late in the afternoon. | People: Lieut. [uncertain]; on these shoots 84 rounds expended; bursts of fire kept up on a line 500° east of S.O.S. line; further concentration placed on W.25.c.28 [uncertain], total 60 rounds fired; battery position heavily shelled, percentage of gas shell observed; one man, No. 2163349 Gunner J. W. Brown, reported slightly gassed and admitted to hospital, otherwise no harm done. | People: Gnr J. W. Brown (No. 2163349). | Casualties: Gnr J. W. Brown slightly gassed.

- **1917-11-03 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Witley) | Witley Camp, Surrey** — All leave cancelled and all ranks recalled. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —
- **1917-11-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Day bright; at 5.05 a.m. an S.O.S. went up and "D" Section's 4 barrage guns opened fire at once, and at 5.45 and 6.15 a.m. the S.O.S. was again sent up by the battalions of the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. holding the front line, the guns firing on S.O.S. lines, several guns having fired 350 rds S.A.A. before the S.O.S. rocket reached the ground, with 13,000 rds S.A.A. expended; enemy shelling was very severe in the early morning, slackening at 8 a.m., about 75 8-inch shells falling near Seine Corner, and enemy aircraft flew low over the lines all afternoon; between 5 and 7 p.m. the enemy put down a heavy barrage with no direct hits on the trench occupied by the barrage guns, but during the bombardment attached carriers Pte. Douville G. and Pte. Davies T.E. were hit and both died of their wounds while being carried to the dressing station; during the night 4,000 rds S.A.A. were fired on Passchendaele crossroads; casualties 2 men killed. | People: Pte. Douville G.; Pte. Davies T.E. | Companies: 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; "D" Section. | Casualties: 2 killed — Pte. Douville G. and Pte. Davies T.E. (attached carriers; died of wounds en route to dressing station).

- **1917-11-04 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Rain in the early morning; at 5 a.m. Lt. Creighton left the transport lines with a pack train of 35 animals loaded with 50,000 rds S.A.A., dumped at Seine Corner, the train returning at 8.15 a.m. with no casualties although the enemy shelled the road near Zonnebek continuously; one crew of "C" Section under Acc. Cpl. Berrick was sent up to report to Lieut. McBurney and placed at D.16.d.55.85 for anti-aircraft work, firing 1,000 rounds at enemy aircraft during the day, and one gun of "D" Section fired 500 rds S.A.A. at an enemy plane which appeared to land behind Passchendaele; during the day, on orders from Capt. Grantham, Lt. McBurney took a party of 8 men to D.11.c.90.30 and began work on a new 8-gun battery position, the party working only 15 minutes before being forced to stop by enemy shelling; between 9 p.m. and midnight 4,000 rds S.A.A. were fired on Passchendaele crossroads; in accordance with 2nd Cdn. Divl. M.G. Battn. O.O. No. 55 para. 6, "B" Section less 1 gun under Lt. Hobson relieved 3 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. (1 gun at D.12.a.45.00, 2 guns at D.12.c.30.70), and 1 gun of "A" Section took up position at D.12.a.30.90 under Sgt. Tingley of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy., relief complete at 10 p.m., all these guns being mobile and under Major Pearce, mobile group commander; during the afternoon the enemy fired 8 5.2-inch high-velocity shells in and about the transport lines; casualties "Nil". | People: Lt. Creighton; Acc. Cpl. Berrick; Lieut. McBurney; Capt. Grantham; Lt. Hobson; Sgt. Tingley. | Companies: "C" Section; "D" Section; "B" Section; "A" Section; 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: none

- **1917-11-05 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Day fine; between 11.30 p.m. 4th inst. and 4.30 this morning the enemy fired about 70 high-velocity 5.2-inch rounds in and about the transport lines, wounding Pte. Larson A.P. (who died later at the dressing station), Pte. Campbell E., Pte. Dills C.E. and Pte. Landry J., while Pte. Wallace A.G. was wounded but remained on duty, and two saddle and two light draught horses were killed and one saddle and eleven light draught horses wounded; enemy aircraft were very active from daybreak all day, a pack train of 25 animals under Sgt. Christie carried 50,000 rds S.A.A. to Seine Corner, the enemy shelled the whole area heavily from 5 to 8 a.m. and shelled the area about "B" Section with heavies during the day, and in "D" Section Pte. Coaton A.C. and Pte. Barrett H. were wounded; Lce. Cpl. Sillers and 8 men of "D" Section worked all day on the new battery position while the remainder carried 33,000 rds S.A.A. to new positions; at 4 p.m. Lt. Gibson left the transport lines with two crews of "A" Section and one crew of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy., taking up positions with the 26th Battn., "D" Section under Lt. McBurney moved to a new position at D.11.c.30.30, and Capt. McCorkell went to advanced 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. headquarters to act as M.G. liaison officer during the operations. | People: Pte. Larson A.P.; Pte. Campbell E.; Pte. Dills C.E.; Pte. Landry J.; Pte. Wallace A.G.; Sgt. Christie; Lce. Cpl. Sillers; Pte. Coaton A.C.; Pte. Barrett H.; Lt. Gibson; Lt. McBurney; Capt. McCorkell. | Companies: "D" Section; "A" Section; 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 26th Battn.; 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. | Casualties: 1 killed — Pte. Larson A.P. (wounded, died later at dressing station); wounded — Pte. Campbell E., Pte. Dills C.E., Pte. Landry J., Pte. Coaton A.C., Pte. Barrett H.; Pte. Wallace A.G. wounded, remained on duty; 2 saddle and 2 light draught horses killed, 1 saddle and 11 light draught horses wounded.
- **1917-11-05 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area** — Fine, scattered clouds, cool; physical drill at 6.30 a.m.; company parade in fighting kit at 9 a.m.; squad drill 10–11 a.m., spare parts gone over 11–12, new guns replacing those damaged in the fighting of 26th and 30th October tested by firing into a bank; at 1.30 p.m. divisional armourer inspected guns, two sent away for slight repairs. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-05 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 10.35 a.m. concentration placed on E9c 15.30, and similar shoot on same target at 2.55 p.m., total 42 rounds fired; barrage Y(a)(b) put up at 4.45 p.m.; in evening further concentrations placed on E7a 91.51, firing 42 rounds; harassing fire on roads leading to Wrath Farm maintained throughout the night, 120 rounds fired; intermittent enemy shelling on battery position 1.00–3.00 p.m. | Locations: Wrath Farm. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-11-06 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Passchendaele** — Rain at intervals; a pack train of 25 animals under Lt. Creighton carried 50,000 rds S.A.A. to Seine Dump; at 6 a.m. the 1st and 2nd Cdn. Div'ns. attacked and captured Passchendaele, the 26th Cdn. Inf. Battn. of the 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. attacking on the right, and the 3 crews under Lt. Gibson advanced with the first wave of the 26th Battn., taking up positions of 2 guns at D.6.d.50.65 and 1 gun at D.6.d.55.05 with no casualties in reaching their objectives, but shortly afterwards Lt. Gibson was wounded by shrapnel in the jaw and over the eye and Sgt. Chamberland took charge; enemy fire was intense all day, in "D" Section Pte. Green H. was killed and Pte. Cook P.R. wounded, barrage guns responded to 3 S.O.S. calls, firing 60,000 rds S.A.A. during barrage and S.O.S. calls and 6,000 rds in harassing fire at night, enemy artillery fire was very heavy from 8 p.m. to midnight, "B" Section on the right was heavily shelled but escaped casualties till 3 p.m., when the right position was practically destroyed, both guns being blown out of the trench, Pte. Osborn A.J. being killed and two of the crew buried but soon dug out by Pte. Wilton R.J. and Pte. Bruce R.B., and the left crew suffered heavily, Pte. Butler T. being killed and Pte. McGrouther R. and Pte. Drysdale wounded. | People: Lt. Creighton; Lt. Gibson; Sgt. Chamberland; Pte. Green H.; Pte. Cook P.R.; Pte. Osborn A.J.; Pte. Wilton R.J.; Pte. Bruce R.B.; Pte. Butler T.; Pte. McGrouther R.; Pte. Drysdale. | Companies: 26th Cdn. Inf. Battn.; 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 1st Cdn. Div.; 2nd Cdn. Div.; "D" Section; "B" Section. | Casualties: 3 killed — Pte. Green H., Pte. Osborn A.J., Pte. Butler T.; wounded — Lt. Gibson (shrapnel, jaw and eye), Pte. Cook P.R., Pte. McGrouther R., Pte. Drysdale.

- **1917-11-06 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — In conjunction with attack by Canadian Divisions this morning at 6 a.m., opened up with attack barrage, immediately followed by protective barrage, maintained up to 3 p.m.; S.O.S. call promptly responded to at 5.40 p.m. and continued until situation again quiet; enemy shelled battery position and vicinity heavily for greater part of day, but did no damage. | Companies: Canadian Divisions. | Casualties: none.

Brutinel (Corps M.G. Officer) and Major Moorhouse (3rd Divisional M.G. Officer) arrived; Lt.-Col. Brutinel congratulated Lieut. - **1917-11-08 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Day fine; a pack train of 25 animals under Lt. Creighton carried 50,000 rds S.A.A. to Seine Corner; enemy shelling was heavy, the "D" Section battery position was hit several times and Pte. Pattison S. and Pte. Collypitts G. were killed; during the night Lt. MacLaren with two guns of "C" Section and 1 gun of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy. relieved the 3 mobile guns of "B" Section under Lt. Hobson, the relieving crews being caught in an enemy barrage on the way in, the two guns of "C" Section being destroyed and Pte. Watkins H. severely wounded, relief complete by 6 p.m. [uncertain] and "B" Section moving back to the transport lines; the 3 guns under Sgt. Chamberland were relieved by 3 guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy., relief complete by 8 p.m., and these crews moved back to the transport lines. | People: Lt. Creighton; Pte. Pattison S.; Pte. Collypitts G.; Lt. MacLaren; Lt. Hobson; Pte. Watkins H.; Sgt. Chamberland. | Companies: "D" Section; "C" Section; 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; "B" Section; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 2 killed — Pte. Pattison S., Pte. Collypitts G.; Pte. Watkins H. severely wounded; 2 guns of "C" Section destroyed.
- **1917-11-08 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area** — Physical drill at 6.30 a.m.; company paraded at 9 a.m. in fighting kit and inspected; sections carried on with mechanism and stripping during the morning; one hour devoted to thorough inspection of gas respirators and S.A.A. helmets; rest of day spent quietly; the two guns returned from being repaired. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-08 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 9 a.m. relieved 35-2 Siege Battery and took up counter-battery work; position now in D.25.b 88.23 on Zonnebeke Road; position extremely poor, very many disadvantages; tasks of minor nature, several bursts of fire, and harassing fire on roads and enemy positions in Moorslede; subjected to very heavy enemy shelling, approximately 1,200 rounds of H.E. and shrapnel, but little damage resulted; only one gun in action, others out for temporary repairs. | Companies: 35-2 Siege Battery. | Locations: Zonnebeke Road; Moorslede. | Casualties: none. | Movement: relieved 35-2 Siege Battery; position D.25.b 88.23.

- **1917-11-08 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Watou** — Light showers; office work in the morning, then in the afternoon inspected the outlying subsections in No. 1 and No. 2 areas and called at the D.D.M.S. office. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-11-09 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | D.11.b.30.30** — Day cool and misty; orders were issued for "D" Section to move forward a thousand yards and take up new battery positions at D.11.b.30.30, and during the day Lt. McBurney went forward, chose a position and had a party dig a trench and emplacements, the guns being put in position at dusk and S.A.A. taken up during the night; the guns under Lt. MacLaren were shelled continuously, with Pte. Hutchings W.J., Pte. Hardiment S.P. and Pte. Miles T.C. killed, and Pte. Tobicoe W., Pte. Gilroy G., Pte. Herter E.F. and Pte. Hindle O.A. wounded. | People: Lt. McBurney; Lt. MacLaren; Pte. Hutchings W.J.; Pte. Hardiment S.P.; Pte. Miles T.C.; Pte. Tobicoe W.; Pte. Gilroy G.; Pte. Herter E.F.; Pte. Hindle O.A. | Companies: "D" Section. | Casualties: 3 killed — Pte. Hutchings W.J., Pte. Hardiment S.P., Pte. Miles T.C.; wounded — Pte. Tobicoe W., Pte. Gilroy G., Pte. Herter E.F., Pte. Hindle O.A. | Movement: "D" Section forward 1,000 yards to D.11.b.30.30.
- **1917-11-09 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area** — Physical drill at 6.30 a.m.; company paraded at 9 a.m. and inspected; paraded again at 10 a.m. and joined the 15th Cdn. M.G. Coy on their parade ground, both companies inspected by Major-General L. J. Lipsett, C.M.G., G.O.C. 3rd Can. Div., at 10.30 a.m.; the General congratulated both companies on their excellent work during the 3rd Divisional attack on Bellevue Spur on 26th and 30th October and the 9th Coy on holding the new line for some time without infantry support; during the afternoon a warning order came in of a move tomorrow; limbers packed as far as possible; during the evening the movement order arrived — move to 'D' Camp just beyond St. Jean; O.C. Major McFaul left for England today on leave of absence (14 days); Lieut. Drinkwater took over command of the company in his absence. | People: Major-General L. J. Lipsett; Major McFaul; Lieut. Drinkwater. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-09 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Shoot on hostile battery at E.W.39 [uncertain] carried out at 5 a.m., 30 rounds fired; at 6 a.m. barrage C(a) commenced and continued till 6.32 a.m.; these were our only shoots this day; enemy artillery secured practically a direct hit on one of our guns and No. 1257506 Sergt W. Rawling was wounded; one gun kept in action, repairs having been effected. | People: Sergt W. Rawling (No. 1257506). | Casualties: Sergt W. Rawling wounded.

- **1917-11-10 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Witley) | Witley Camp, Surrey** — Routine day; overcast, cold. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —
- **1917-11-10 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Field** — Rain during the day; at 6.05 a.m. the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. of the 2nd Cdn. Div., in conjunction with the 1st Cdn. Div. and the 1st Imperial Division, attacked the enemy's position under cover of an intense barrage, the 1st and 2nd Cdn. Div. gaining all their objectives while the 1st Imperial Division on the left was held up, the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. meeting no resistance but the 1st Cdn. Div. meeting considerable; the barrage guns fired 14,000 rds S.A.A. during the attack and 4,500 rds on the S.O.S. call at 3 p.m., and during the afternoon rain fell heavily and the positions were nearly washed away. | People: — | Companies: 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 1st Cdn. Div.; 1st Imperial Division. | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area → E Camp, St. Jean** — Everyone up by 4.30 a.m.; it had rained heavily through the night and rain came down again heavily as the company marched off about 6.30 a.m.; met convoy of busses on the Watou-Abeele road and embussed at K 18 b; the 7th, 8th and 15th M.G. Coys also moved by this convoy, and the 43rd, 1st C.M.R. Bns., [uncertain] T.M.B. and Bde. HQ; by 7.45 a.m. all settled in the busses to the Asylum in Ypres, where they left the conveyances and marched to camp — D Camp was too small for the four companies and E Camp was allotted to us (C 27 d); housed partly in huts and partly in tents; transport left lines at 9.15 a.m. via Poperinghe, Vlamertinghe and Salvation Corner, arriving about 2 p.m.; ground deep with mud and water, but everyone settled by dark with a good hot dinner; many heavy guns in the vicinity active through the night, some enemy shelling a few hundred yards in our rear. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Watou area → E Camp, St. Jean (by bus via Ypres).
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — One gun opened up in response to S.O.S. call at 2.50 p.m., 10 rounds fired; several bursts of fire placed in W.26.d, about 45 rounds expended; eventually stopped by enemy neutralising fire, unusually heavy; no damage done, gun went into action again later; during night maintained fire on enemy roads, gun positions, etc. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-11-10 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Brandhoek Area, France** — Received from Headquarters, 2nd Canadian Infantry Brigade, 1 Stewart clipper with 2 clipper heads; no horses admitted. | Casualties: none.

Orders to prepare to hand over 20 miles and 5 sappers to the new 11th & 12th Battalions. Lieut. R. P. Williams [uncertain] of B Coy awarded the Military Cross. | People: Lieut. R. P. Williams [uncertain] (Military Cross). | Companies: B Coy.

- **1917-11-11 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Field** — Day fine; the 4 crews of "D" Section were withdrawn at 7 a.m. and reported back to the transport lines, their guns, tripods and 22 belts and boxes being taken back by mule train, and the 3 guns under Lt. MacLaren were relieved by three guns of the 11th Cdn. M.G. Coy. and withdrew to the transport lines, arriving back about midnight; the 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy. moved into the transport lines in the afternoon, and the 4th Cdn. Div. is relieving the 2nd Cdn. Div. in the line, relief to be completed by the morning of the 13th. | People: Lt. MacLaren. | Companies: "D" Section; 11th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 4th Cdn. Div. | Casualties: none | Movement: "D" Section and Lt. MacLaren's guns withdrawn to transport lines.
- **1917-11-11 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | E Camp, St. Jean** — Fine today with one or two light showers; accommodation made more comfortable, men cleaned up revolvers and rifles in the morning; enemy shelled the area intermittently during the day with H.V. shells and shrapnel; the 15th Cdn. M.G. relieved 8 guns each by the 13th and 3rd [uncertain] in Battery No. 5 (D 11 a) and Battery No. 6 (D 5 c); four guns of the 8th [uncertain] relieved four guns of the 3rd [uncertain] in Battery No. 7 (D 5 c), and four guns of the 7th [uncertain] relieved four guns of the 13th [uncertain] in the same battery; Capt. Hartley of 15th [uncertain] in command of barrage guns at Capitol; Lieut. Burnham liaison officer at Korbek. | People: Capt. Hartley; Lieut. Burnham. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-11 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Moorslede subjected to 16 rounds rapid fire at 6.45 a.m.; no other targets during the day; from 9 p.m. onwards through the night harassing fire kept up on enemy positions at E3a 20.5 and E26.5-6; battery position again subjected to heavy enemy fire, secured direct hits on "pillboxes" in which detachments had taken cover; as a result 2 casualties (shell shock) — A/Sgt R. J. Taylor and Gnr H. Spinney; billets also subjected to hostile shelling and one shell smashed in a cellar used as telephone cabinet; as a result one casualty, Gunner M. R. Jones, and communication to group and battery temporarily broken; Lt. A. C. Kray [uncertain] proceeded on leave to England this date. | People: A/Sgt R. J. Taylor; Gnr H. Spinney; Gnr M. R. Jones; Lt. A. C. Kray. | Locations: Moorslede. | Casualties: A/Sgt R. J. Taylor and Gnr H. Spinney (shell shock); Gnr M. R. Jones wounded.

- **1917-11-12 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Fosse 10, France** — Draft of reinforcements arrived in the lines today, in accordance with G.H.Q. letter 6697 (Q.A.1) of 8th Oct. 1917: 1 C.Q.M.S., 1 driver wheeler, 2 driver saddlers, 1 farrier sergeant, 2 driver farriers, 18 drivers [uncertain], 1 staff sergeant (clerk), 1 clerk, 3 issuers and 1 butcher; the subaltern called for by the letter has not yet arrived, being at Base doing conducting duty, and great rejoicing among all ranks meeting old friends. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-12 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Witley) | Witley Camp, Surrey** — Lieut. Maw reports. | People: Lieut. Maw | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —
- **1917-11-12 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Brandhoek** — In accordance with 2nd Cdn. Divl. M.G. Battn. O.O. No. 60 tables "A" and "B", the transport left the Potijze area at 6 a.m. and proceeded via Vlaemertinghe, Busseboom, Abeele and Godewaersvelde to Eecke, where they parked for the night, while the company less transport moved off from the Potijze area at 11.45 a.m., entrained at Ypres station at 12.30 p.m. and proceeded by train to Brandhoek, detraining and marching to a camp of tents at H.14.c.10 on the Poperinghe and Renninghelst road. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Potijze area–Brandhoek (company by train via Ypres); transport to Eecke.
- **1917-11-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | E Camp, St. Jean** — Fine but misty and a little warmer; 20 men under Sgt. Lewis left camp at 6.10 a.m. with 3 limbers and 10 mules to Waterloo, carrying S.A.A. to barrage positions and returning at 3.30 p.m.; quiet in the line, very little shelling; guns and equipment thoroughly gone over and cleaned up, new guns tried out; moved transport lines and company during the afternoon to the 3rd [uncertain]'s lines at C 26 d, remaining in our hut in E Camp for some of the officers; some shelling of the area last night and at 6 a.m., a little more during the day; the 8th [uncertain] relieved 10 guns (4 of the 2nd [uncertain] in advanced position and 6 of the 1st [uncertain]) at D 6 a, V 30 c and D 5 b. | People: Sgt. - **1917-11-14 to 1917-11-19 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — No guns arrived from workshop yet; opportunity taken to improve battery position and commence a new one; work frequently interrupted by hostile shell fire, and during this period two small cartridge dumps blown up; no other damage done and no casualties caused; letters of appreciation received from G.O.C.R.A. Canadian Corps (Army Commander's appreciation of artillery's splendid work in the Passchendaele operations) and from General Commanding 2nd Army, Gen. H. Plumer — "I should be glad if you would express to all Brigades, Groups and Batteries of Artillery who have served in the 2nd Army throughout the offensive operations this summer + autumn, my appreciation of the splendid work they have done — I fully realise how arduous this work has been. I know that they have suffered heavy losses, and have had to remain in action under the most trying circumstances for very long periods — They have never flinched or abated their efforts for a moment but have steadily continued to overcome all difficulties, and as a result they have contributed very materially to the success achieved." | People: Gen. H. Plumer. | Companies: Canadian Corps; 2nd Army. | Casualties: none.

Caldwell relieved two guns of the 15th [uncertain] in Battery position No. 6 (D 5 c); 12 guns of the 7th [uncertain] relieved 12 guns of the 15th Coy in battery positions 5 and 6; 14 guns of the 8th Coy were relieved by 14 guns of the 9th Coy in forward positions — A Section under Lieut. Hulbert took 6 guns (D 5 a and 2 guns B Section) to positions at D 5 b; relief carried out without a casualty; Lieut. - **1917-11-16 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Passchendaele** — Fine, mild; rations brought up by carrying party; just after getting a gun into position last [uncertain] at D 6 b the shelter containing Pte. Burnett and Pte. McGregor was hit with a shell and both were killed; Pte. Shields of B Section was slightly wounded by a shell falling near the position; during the day the gun crew in position V 30 c was put out of action by shell — Ptes. McLean, Boyle and McNounn were wounded and gun and equipment lost; crew at Waterloo brought up to replace them and placed in position a short distance from the old position; shelling of the forward area pretty heavy all day, and the Meetcheele–Bellevue Road so constantly shelled there is very little of it left; during the evening the right flank of the Corps on our left advanced without artillery preparation and captured Vocation Farm by a surprise attack. | People: Pte. Burnett; Pte. McGregor; Pte. Shields; Pte. McLean; Pte. Boyle; Pte. McNounn. | Companies: B Section. | Casualties: Pte. Burnett and Pte. McGregor killed; Pte. Shields slightly wounded; Ptes. - **1917-11-25 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — One gun now in action; first shoot at 7.30 p.m. on S.O.S. lines in response to S.O.S. call; during night harassing fire on enemy roads maintained; total rounds fired 60; O.C. desires to place on record excellent work of gun detachments on 8th and 9th, and especially good examples set by No. 1 Sergeants Palmer, Mosley and Rawling in their untiring efforts not only to put, but to keep the only available gun in action throughout the night, under very adverse circumstances; Sgt. - **1917-12-03 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Barlin** — Fine, very cold; company paraded at 9 a.m., morning spent with squad drill, stoppages and immediate action, and gas drill; a special class started today for officers and N.C.O.s of the four M.G. - **1917-12-23 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Barlin → Quarries** — Limbers packed and company paraded in full marching order at 8.15 a.m. ready to move out; A, B and C Sections moved off to the line via Bully Grenay, halting there for a rest and meal before completing the journey to the trenches; D, Headquarters and Transport moved off towards Mazingarbe, reached about noon; after a few hours rest those going to the trenches again moved off via Bully Grenay, Maroc and Loos; company HQ established in the Quarries at M 6 a, HQ of the 33rd M.G. Coy., and gun positions taken over at M 18 b, N 4 c, N 8 d, N 8 c, N 9 b, N 9 a, N 8 a, N 4 a and N 1 c/d; relief carried through without incident and all complete by 11 p.m.; transport stayed overnight at Mazingarbe and moved next day to permanent lines at Les Brebis. | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Barlin → Quarries (via Bully Grenay, Maroc, Loos); transport → Mazingarbe.

- **1918-01-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — At 3.10 a.m. the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion carried out a successful raid with the assistance of artillery, trench mortars and machine guns; they entered the enemy's trenches at H 32 d and H 25 d, securing 2 prisoners belonging to 2nd Coy, 1st Battn., 213th R.I.R., and suffered very light casualties, only four men slightly wounded; a number of dugouts were bombed and casualties inflicted; our part consisted of covering all approaches to the points of entry — 9 of our machine guns with the assistance of 6 guns of the 1st Motor M.G. Brigade fired 3,650 rounds from 2.10 a.m. until 3 a.m.; a strange thing happened when Sergt. Bullock was firing a gun at N 1 a: he had only fired 250 rounds when an enemy bullet struck the [uncertain] on the crank handle, breaking it off and slightly wounding the sergeant in the hand, and another bullet pierced the [uncertain] of the muzzle cup, putting the gun out of action; the sergeant remained on duty; situation normal during the balance of the day, usual artillery exchanges, trench mortar work and machine-gun fire; two enemy planes over our lines in the morning and three of ours over on his side. | People: Sergt. Bullock. | Casualties: Sergt. Bullock slightly wounded in the hand; 2 prisoners taken (enemy, 213th R.I.R.). | Movement: —
- **1918-01-12 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Thelus, France** — Gun positions: 2 guns at Angres, 4 at Petit Vimy; work now wholly counter-battery. Aeroplane shoot attempted but given up after 10 rounds through engine trouble of the plane. Four N.F. calls answered on targets OY36, OY28, OY29 and NX63, 100 rounds fired; Angres section fired 25 rounds on target H8 NX63. Enemy artillery fairly quiet. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-01-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — Cold and clear; observation planes on both sides busy; scouting planes indulged in three [uncertain]; a new feature today — one of our Stokes trench mortars fired 20 rounds at a Hun plane that found the high altitudes too cold and sought a warmer level; 2 enemy balloons up from 9 a.m. to 12 noon; one of the entrances of a dugout at N 1 b occupied by a gun crew of C Section was blown in by a 4.1" at 5 p.m.; at 11.40 a.m. enemy heavily bombarded the east side of Loos for eight minutes; usual artillery, trench mortar and machine-gun activity. | Companies: C Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1918-01-14 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Nedonchelle** — The company paraded at 1 p.m. and marched to Nedonchelle, where the battalion under Major Goodfellow, M.C. was inspected by Brigadier General Ketchen at 2 p.m.; the appearance of the men was very good and the equipment clean and well fitted, the brigadier giving a thorough inspection with special attention to arms and ammunition, after which a demonstration of gas drill was given under Lieut. Colonel McIntyre, several movements in company drill were carried out, and the inspecting officer congratulated the commanding officer on the efficiency of his company and awarded him first place in the battalion; the company returned to Nedon at 4 p.m., where a company inspection was held by the O.C., "A" Section being chosen as the cleanest and most soldier-like section, and the transport section under Lieut. Robson marched to Aux Reitz. | People: Major Goodfellow, M.C.; Brigadier General Ketchen; Lieut. Colonel McIntyre; Lieut. Robson. | Companies: "A" Section. | Casualties: none
- **1918-01-14 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — A snowfall of two or three inches during the early hours affords a welcome relief to the eyes; situation normal; A Battery under Lieut. Adams, 1st C.M. M.G. Brigade, relieved by B Battery of the same unit at 6 p.m. under Lieut. Trench; all preparations made and calculations checked for the coming raid; the 5th C.M.R. Battalion carried out what was to be a 'stealth' raid at 11 p.m. — raiding party of 2 officers and 26 O.R.s penetrated the German line at H 32 d, captured 2 prisoners of the 209th R.I.R. and one machine gun, suffering only 1 O.R. wounded; the idea was to cut the wire by hand and carry on without assistance, failing this a T.M. rocket (red-green-red) was to be fired calling for a 'box' barrage; promptly at 11.30 p.m. the signal rocket went up and all arms immediately responded — we fired 15,000 rounds in 30 minutes in answer to this call; in view of an anticipated German relief during the night 7,750 more rounds were fired on the main avenues of approach. | People: Lieut. Adams; Lieut. Trench. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded (5th C.M.R.); 2 prisoners and 1 machine gun captured (enemy, 209th R.I.R.). | Movement: —

Division, our Coy is in Army Reserve; beyond a rifle range and a long range for indirect fire close by, this area has very little to commend it for a combined rest-training period, with absolutely no form of amusement for the men; Capt. - **1918-03-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy defences** — Situation quiet; low visibility on account of heavy ground mist until about noon; orders received from D.M.G.C. 3rd Cdn. (Appendix 2, O.O. No. X, undated: all sections to man battle positions immediately; Appendix 3, report on the operation of 13.3.18, dated 14 Mar: practice "Stand To" a success, no previous warning given; gun crews knew their positions, but officers away from sections did not always leave an N.C.O. definitely in charge, and in two cases gun mounts had to be torn out as not properly built.) | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

Brutinell for all ranks to be fed and stand to ready to move off at any time after 6 am Friday morning. | People: Capt. G. Black; Col. Brutinell; Gen. (Oppy) quickly responded to at 6 a.m., 41 rounds fired; N.F. calls very frequent throughout the day, about 150 rounds fired; at 1.05 p.m. a further S.O.S. (Oppy) answered, 53 rounds fired; during the night, 50 rounds expended harassing fire on enemy roads; rear section became active and opened up on the same S.O.S., firing 51 rounds, and responded to N.F. calls during the night; Thelus (billet) very heavily shelled throughout the day, as was Vimy and Petit Vimy, and roads [entry ends mid-sentence]. | Casualties: none.

W. Sharp. | Companies: 4th Cdn Div. | Casualties: **A few company men — casualties in the 28 March battle, none serious (no names given)**

- **1918-04-15 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — 30 rounds harassing fire on various H.B. positions 6–7 a.m.; two shoots of neutralizing fire on H.B. at U.8.b.11.9, 55 rounds fired; during the night 60 rounds harassing fire on H.B.s at O.25.c and O.35.c. At about 10 a.m. the enemy commenced shelling position S.24.d., firing about 20 rounds H.E., apparently for ranging; at 2.30 p.m. a heavy bombardment on the same location, about 200 rounds; one shell burst in No. 1 gun pit, in which Lieut. E. A. MacKenzie and the gun crew were working. Lieut. E. A. MacKenzie (severely wounded), Bombr. J. T. Wentzell (killed), Gnr. E. C. Parslow (died of wounds), Gnr. C. G. Leroux (died of wounds), Gnr. L. L. Lawrence (severely wounded), Gnr. J. Barclay (died of wounds), Gnr. Croft (wounded), Gnr. Bateman (severely wounded) and Gnr. A. N. Matheson (wounded); no material was damaged. | People: Lieut. Matheson. | Casualties: 4 killed/died of wounds (Bombr. Wentzell; Gnrs. Parslow, Leroux, Barclay); 5 wounded (Lieut. MacKenzie; Gnrs. Lawrence, Croft, Bateman, Matheson).

- **1918-05-02 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Aux-Rietz, France** — Clear and mild; two remounts received from Can. Corps; L.D.s for limber wagon, indented for brigades. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

[uncertain]. | Companies: 1st, 2nd and 3rd Field Ambulances; 4th Division. | Casualties: none

- **1918-05-21 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Frevin Capelle, France** — Moved the company to Frevin Capelle; railhead Houdain, a beautiful day, and left the lines in Houdain at 2.30 p.m., arriving Frevin Capelle at 6 p.m. on a very hot day; cleared the pack train the same as usual in the morning, dumping and handing the same over to the S.D.O. 4th Cdn. Div., with No. 1 Coy. 4th Cdn. Div. carrying out the same plan in conjunction with the arrangements, and no lorries used for the move, the company supply wagons moving empty; a bomb dropped near 5th C.D.A. Battalion (A.G. 4th letter K.E. 28764/Y, 21-5-18). | People: Dr. Cody J.M. (469194); Dr. Nicholson J.M. (301296). | Companies: No. 1 Coy. 1st Cdn. Divl. Train; 85th Cdn. - **1918-07-31 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Bouquemaison / Hornoy, France** — The dismounted party marched from Bouquemaison at 6 a.m. to entrain at Doullens, one O.R. slightly crushing his foot under a wagon wheel, the party boarded the train at 10.15 a.m. and arrived at Saleux at 2.45 p.m., and was then transported to Hornoy, 33 kilometres west of Amiens, where the office was opened in a barn with D.R.L.S. communication and one sounder line to Canadian Corps. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: **1 O.R. — foot slightly crushed under a wagon wheel** | Movement: Bouquemaison–Doullens–Saleux–Hornoy.

- **1918-08-07 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arras** — Inspected cellars in Arras; great improvement — permission obtained to operate incinerators on dull days. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-08 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Training all day; Reinforcements No. 246 (15 Other Ranks 25th Battalion, 79 Other Ranks 85th Battalion, 10 Other Ranks R.C.R.) proceeded overseas at 11 p.m.; Lt. Col. C. L. E. Willetts, D.S.O., O.C. Royal Canadian Regiment in the Field, visited the unit, inspecting training and troops; 103 Other Ranks reported from and 113 proceeded to Mytchett Musketry Camp. | People: Lt. Col. C. L. E. Willetts, D.S.O. | Companies: 25th Battalion; 85th Battalion; Royal Canadian Regiment; N.S.R.D. | Locations: Mytchett Musketry Camp.
- **1918-08-08 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Domart, France** — The battle commenced at 4.20 a.m. with a heavy short bombardment, many tanks and aeroplanes, telephonic communication was lost with the brigades from the start, visual signalling became effective after the dust and smoke cleared, cable wagons followed the brigades where possible, and towards evening Divisional and Brigade HQs grouped in Valley Wood with good telephone communication before moving to Hamel Wood, with 2 O.Rs. casualties for the day and Capt. K.M. Campbell taking over command. | People: Capt. K.M. Campbell. | Companies: — | Casualties: **2 O.Rs. — casualties for the day** | Movement: Domart–Valley Wood–Hamel Wood.
- **1918-08-08 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Plachy Buyon** — If the attack gains its objectives the Train may move forward to Boves and M.T. will come into use again, as the long haul over very bad roads is telling on the horses; at 2 p.m. orders came to move at once to Bois de Gentelles, then changed to Domart owing to the success of the advance. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: ordered to Domart.
- **1918-08-08 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Gentille Wood, France** — Fine and warm; zero hour 4 am; all lines O.K. during the show, never out of telephonic communication; 10.00 am 5th C.D.A. out of action and held in reserve. (Battle of Amiens.) | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-08 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Cagny to T2C 5.8** — Company moved from Cagny at 7 p.m., arriving 12 p.m.; supply lorries failed to report at the railhead, an oversight Capt. Cole rectified. | People: Capt. Cole | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Cagny to T2C 5.8
- **1918-08-08 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Near Souchez, France** — Bombardment of enemy positions in houses at N22c.36.48 carried out with ground observation during the afternoon, 200 rounds fired, shoot reported very satisfactory, O.K.s observed; harassing fire carried out on targets at N29c.50.99 and N29a.60.50 during the night, 75 rounds fired. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-08 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | St. Fluchien, France** — Ambulance returns to [uncertain], collecting one horse (Billet No. 9). Admitted 3 horses to M.V.S. Section moves from Vers to St. Fluchien. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Vers to St. Fluchien.
- **1918-08-08 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arras** — To Dainville, Wagnonlieu and Longuez [uncertain]; sanitary conditions more satisfactory; office work. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-09 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Training in morning; afternoon route march per Operation Order No. 38; 10 Other Ranks struck off strength proceeding overseas to R.C.R., 15 to 25th Battalion, 7 to 85th Battalion. | Companies: Royal Canadian Regiment; 25th Battalion; 85th Battalion.
- **1918-08-09 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Valley Wood / Beaucourt, France** — The infantry still went forward and Divisional HQ advanced towards Beaucourt, motor cyclists worked very hard giving adequate service to all units, telephone communication was established for the past 12 hours to the brigades with six lines [uncertain — "ix"] used entirely by "G" Staff, and HQ was taken up for the night in Beaucourt Chateau with casualties nil. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Valley Wood–Beaucourt.
- **1918-08-09 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Domart** — Train Headquarters moved at 9 a.m. to Domart; at 3 p.m. all Train companies moved forward halfway between Domart and Maison Blanche, on the road from Moreuil to Demuin, contour 104, 1½ miles south of Demuin, where all supply dumps are also located. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: to Domart, then to the road between Domart and Maison Blanche.
- **1918-08-09 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Gentille Wood, France** — Fine; brigades moved to Domart Wood; order received at 10.00 pm to move forward under 32nd Division. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: brigades to Domart Wood.
- **1918-08-09 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | U13 C 1.6** — Company moved off at 8.15 a.m. to U13 C 1.6; lorries dumped there the next morning; O.C. visited ground captured the previous day [uncertain — entry partly cut off]. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: T2C 5.8 to U13 C 1.6
- **1918-08-09 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Near Souchez, France** — At 3 p.m. a bombardment of enemy position at N29a.80.40 commenced with ground observation, shoot completed successfully, 200 rounds fired, Observing Officer reports several O.K.s on target; 65 rounds harassing fire during the night on targets at N29a.20.20 and N35a.25.24; from 11.30 p.m., 44 rounds fired in accordance with D.A. Order No. 26 on targets at N20a.43.57 and N12c.10.73. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-09 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Gentelles Wood, France** — Transferred to No. 10 M.V.S., B.E.F. [uncertain], 10 horses. Section moves from St. Fluchien to Gentelles Wood (T.10. d.7.6, Sheet 62 D). No. 34730 Sergt. Salmon J. rejoins unit from First Army Rest Camp. Ambulance rejoins unit from Hornoy with Case 165. | People: No. 34730 Sergt. Salmon J. | Casualties: 10 horses transferred to No. 10 M.V.S. | Movement: St. Fluchien to Gentelles Wood.
- **1918-08-09 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arras** — Arras; 2 large brick incinerators now erected to replace corrugated iron structures out of repair and not sufficient to handle refuse of town; called on Town Commandant; to Dury [uncertain] for cash. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-10 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Training in morning; 38 Other Ranks taken on strength from N.S.R.D. (reporting from 2nd C.C. Depot); 1 officer struck off strength on transfer to 13th Canadian Reserve Battalion. | Companies: 13th Canadian Reserve Battalion; No. 1 Detachment, Canadian Ordnance Corps, Ashford; N.S.R.D.
- **1918-08-10 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Le Quesnel, France** — Headquarters opened at Le Quesnel at 9 a.m., captured from the enemy at noon on the 9th, Advanced Signals were 1,000 yards east of the village in a French cement pill-box with the rear office in the basement of the badly damaged Chateau, the 7th and 9th C.I. Bdes. were relieved by two brigades of the 32nd Imperial Division, enemy aircraft bombed the rear areas, 4 horses were killed by enemy bombs and 1 by shell fire, and Lieut. J.D. Baker reported for duty to fill the vacancy caused by the death of Lieut. R.W. Auld [uncertain]. | People: Lieut. J.D. Baker; Lieut. R.W. Auld [uncertain]. | Companies: 7th C.I. Bde.; 9th C.I. Bde.; 32nd Imperial Div. | Casualties: **4 horses — killed by enemy bombs; 1 horse — killed by enemy shell fire** | Movement: Beaucourt–Le Quesnel.
- **1918-08-10 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Demuin road camp** — The O.C. tried three cases in No. 2 Company before moving; he saw the A.A.Q.M.G. and gathered the Train was not likely to have to deliver beyond Quesnel, so it will remain in camp, where the hauls are long but mostly downhill with loaded wagons and water for horses is over a mile away. | People: — | Companies: No. 2 Company. | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-10 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Beaucourt / Beaufort, France** — Fine and warm; 5th C.D.A. moved off at 4 am and joined 32nd Division as their artillery at Beaucourt [uncertain spelling]; battle H.Q. established at L 13 b. 50; visual and telephonic communication with brigades and batteries, also lines with infantry, established by 4 pm; rear H.Q. at Beaufort; [uncertain] Douglas M.C. became a casualty. | People: Douglas, M.C. | Companies: 32nd Division. | Casualties: **Douglas, M.C. — became a casualty (nature not stated)**. | Movement: to Beaucourt; rear H.Q. at Beaufort.
- **1918-08-10 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | K7 B 3.7** — Company moved off at 8.30 a.m., loaded, to K7 B 3.7, arriving about 11.30 a.m.; bombing very severe; Dvr. Warwick (on command to 55th Battery) and 2 H.D. horses killed by an enemy bomb, Warwick buried at Beaufort Church. | People: Dvr. Warwick A. | Companies: 55th Battery | Casualties: Dvr. Warwick A. killed by enemy bomb; 2 H.D. horses killed | Movement: U13 C 1.6 to K7 B 3.7
- **1918-08-10 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Near Souchez, France** — Railway Cutting at N28c.50.70 bombarded from 11.45 a.m., observed by No. 10 Balloon and Observing Officer at Hawk O.P., 200 rounds fired, reported very successful, many O.K.s observed; 65 rounds harassing fire on targets at N28b.47.40 and N29c.59.20. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-10 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Gentelles Wood, France** — Paperwork only. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arras** — Paid unit; received orders from XVII Corps at 8 p.m. that lorry would report at 9 a.m. tomorrow to move stores and personnel to train, then moving to 4th Army. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-11 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — No training; tour of duty as Duty Battalion ended, taken over by 13th Canadian Reserve Battalion; Divine Services in morning. | Companies: 13th Canadian Reserve Battalion.
- **1918-08-11 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Demuin road camp** — The Hun bombed all around during the night but there were no casualties to the Train, though the D.A.C. close by got it badly; Division Headquarters was located at Quesnel, 600 horses were reported captured by Cavalry at Roye, and Train Headquarters moved into a dug-out close to No. 1 Company. | People: — | Companies: No. 1 Company. | Casualties: none (Train); D.A.C. hit badly
- **1918-08-11 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Le Quesnel, France** — Fine; rear H.Q. moved to Le Quesnel; line run into 3rd Can. Div. exchange, thus giving us communication with advanced H.Q. as well as Adm. Corps [uncertain]. | People: — | Companies: 3rd Can. Div. | Casualties: none | Movement: Beaufort–Le Quesnel.
- **1918-08-11 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | K7 B 3.7** — Several batteries made local moves; Pte. Orton J. wounded by enemy machine-gun fire | Movement: —
- **1918-08-11 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Near Souchez, France** — Bombardment of enemy dugouts at N21.d.00.92 carried out 1.30–4 p.m., 150 rounds fired, observer reports shoot very satisfactory; at 5.09 a.m. an "xx" call received, no rounds fired, target beyond range; 35 rounds harassing fire on target at N34b.65.97. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-11 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Caix, France** — Transferred 2 horses to No. 10 M.V.S., B.E.F. [uncertain]. Section moves from Gentelles Wood to Caix. | Casualties: 2 horses transferred to No. 10 M.V.S. | Movement: Gentelles Wood to Caix.
- **1918-08-11 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arras** — Two lorries reported and took stores and personnel to Agnez Dure [uncertain] railhead; train left 3.30 p.m.; Chapman went with Ford car and reported to D.O.M.S. - **1918-08-12 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Training as usual; tug-of-war team qualified for the O.M.F. of C. - **1918-08-12 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Le Quesnel, France** — The 3rd Canadian Division was now in Corps reserve, everything ran satisfactorily, German signalling equipment, switchboards, telephones, wire drums and disused wire were salvaged, and considerable enemy bombing last night caused damage to lines. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-12 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Demuin road camp** — General Lipsett passed on Sir Douglas Haig's congratulations to the Division; volunteers were sought for Siberia, Capt. Bawlf and the Interpreter reported back from Boves, and the A.A.&Q.M.G. and D.A.Q.M.G. expressed entire satisfaction with the Train's work in the recent operations. | People: Gen. L. J. Lipsett; Sir Douglas Haig; Capt. Bawlf. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-12 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Le Quesnel, France** — Fine and very warm; situation quiet; unable to obtain new motorcycle from either 3rd or 4th Cdn. Div. or S.M.T.O., thus leaving us without a motorcycle; during the night of 11th–12th Sgt. A.R. Mawdsley [uncertain surname] and Cpl. E. Nash were recommended for decoration for their splendid work which enabled their brigade commander to keep in close touch with the infantry and the general situation which at the time was so critical. | People: Sgt. A. R. Mawdsley [uncertain]; Cpl. E. Nash. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-12 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | K7 B 3.7** — Owing to bombing and exposed lines, O.C. reconnoitred ground further back, nothing suitable; visited batteries in the morning; bombing bad. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —
- **1918-08-12 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Near Souchez, France** — No tasks during the day; harassing fire on enemy roads at N29a.60.50 and N35d.20.80 carried out during the night, 65 rounds fired. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-08-12 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Caix, France** — Capt. Smallland [uncertain] P. assumes command of the unit. No. 19994 Pte. H. E. Brooks, 1st Cdn. Div. - **1918-08-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Boves** — Unit arrived at Longeau Station 2 a.m.; no transportation provided but borrowed a lorry from nearby unit and arrived at Boves; got billets and looked over town, which was in a filthy condition — civilian population evacuated, troops billeted in houses all very dirty and littered with refuse. | Casualties: none. | Movement: arrived at Boves.
- **1918-08-13 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Training as usual; heavy demands for reinforcements for 26th, 85th Battalions and R.C.R.; 12 Other Ranks proceeded on command to Aldershot to act as camp details opening a new segregation camp; 6 cadets who completed the 9th Officers' Training Class at C.T.S., Bexhill-on-Sea, taken on strength as officers (effect 6 August). | Companies: 26th Battalion; 85th Battalion; Royal Canadian Regiment; Canadian Training School, Bexhill-on-Sea; N.S.R.D. | Locations: Aldershot.
- **1918-08-13 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Le Quesnel, France** — Ideal weather had prevailed since the commencement of operations, there was no change in dispositions, communication to all brigades was good with all front-line battalions linked by telephone, and 7th Brigade Section made successful experiments with German homing pigeons captured near the village of Le Folies [uncertain]. | People: — | Companies: 7th Bde. | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-13 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Demuin road camp** — Weekly mileage 9,918 miles; General Lipsett forwarded the Division's casualties to noon yesterday (76 officers, 1,487 other ranks) and prisoners (2,915 all ranks); Captains de Graves and Fisher volunteered for Siberia. | People: Gen. Lipsett; W. W. Gibsone; Capt. de Graves; Capt. Fisher. | Companies: Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4 Companies. | Casualties: Division 76 officers, 1,487 O.R.s (not Train)
- **1918-08-13 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Le Quesnel, France** — Fine and warm; situation unchanged; rear H.Q. shelled out of Le Quesnel village; Sapper W. Pace and Sapper M. G. Henderson were recommended for decoration; these men with absolute disregard for danger maintained flag visual station and lines in the face of the enemy and heavy shelling, enabling their brigade commander to keep in touch with the situation and transmit very valuable information to the rear as a heavy counter-attack by the enemy was imminent. | People: Sapper W. Pace; Sapper M. G. Henderson. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-08-13 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | K7 B 3.7** — Visited batteries; witnessed one of our planes brought down over the battery lines by 8 enemy aircraft; moved the company across the road into thick wood. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: company moved across road into thick wood

- **1918-08-13 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Caix, France** — No. 18453 Dvr. Murray J. J. admitted to No. 33 C.C.S. Destroyed today Cases 186 and 190 (shrapnel wounds). No. 16571 Pte. - **1918-08-14 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Demuin road camp** — S.S.O. to railhead; besides ordnance and mails the Train must now bring back salvage, with no wagon to be loaded with more than 1,000 lbs. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

Gibson continued his poled cable line to these HQs, completing it at 10 a.m., poled cable proved much better than hastily laid overland lines, wire trouble in the afternoon was cleared by 5 p.m., and the Division was relieved by 4th British Division, relief complete at 6.30 p.m., with all personnel except one office relief and Lieut. - **1918-09-24 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Villers-Cagnicourt, France** — 200-round shoot on wire cutting carried out today, ground observation, wire reported badly damaged but not destroyed; further 400 rounds fired into this wire with good results; enemy shelled vicinity of V.4.d with 5.9 H.E., firing about 30 rounds; at 10 p.m. bombardments commenced in connection with Operation Order No. 4, gas and H.E. used, targets Sauchicourt Farm and Wood, Dartford Wood and Area E, 168 rounds fired in all. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-09-27 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Bourlon / Quarry Wood, France** — Zero at 5.20; lines all O.K. and remained in throughout the barrage at zero plus 6 hours and 51 minutes; brigades limbered up and moved just over the canal E15 (sheet 57C); O.C. went forward to locate forward H.Q.s with 9th C.I.B. in front of Quarry Wood; no dugouts available, so H.Q.s established at E9 C1.9 and lines rear to both brigades and 9th C.I.B., where C.R.A. and Brigade Major remained for the night. | People: C.R.A.; Brigade Major. | Companies: 9th C.I.B. | Casualties: none | Movement: across Canal du Nord to Bourlon area.

[uncertain] | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —
- **1918-09-27 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Villers-Cagnicourt, France** — In connection with offensive operations, barrage fire commenced at 5.20 a.m. and continued until 11.08 a.m., firing 1,404 rounds; while the barrage was in progress, 3 guns moved up into position west of Baralle Wood and were in action by 1 p.m., two guns moved into this position later, 1 gun remaining for repairs; all guns in position and ready for action by 3 p.m.; heavy bombardment of enemy post at Oisy-le-Verger and Area K then carried out in connection with 11th Div. Order No. 134, 336 rounds fired. | Companies: 11th Div. | Casualties: none. | Movement: 5 guns forward to west of Baralle Wood.

- **1918-09-28 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | E. 11. c. 0.0. / V. 26. d. 7.9., France** — There was a great deal of line trouble during the night from shell fire and heavy traffic, cable lines were poled from D. 4. d. 7.9 to the Report Centre at E. 10. b. 3.9 under Captain Leeson with 20 men from 9th Battalion C.E., the Division was notified at 9.30 a.m. that it was moving to E. 11. c. 0.0, two lines were run there from the Report Centre by 11 a.m., the Division closed at D. 4. d. 7.9 at 3 p.m., and Military Medals for operations in August 1918 were awarded to 107184 Sgt. A. Dunbar, 107325 Spr. W.C. Impett, 504315 Cpl. C.A. Ryder, 312021 Spr. F.J. Manson, 110276 Spr. R.H. Johnson and 892117 Spr. J.L. Patterson. | People: Capt. Leeson; Sgt. A. Dunbar; Spr. W.C. Impett; Cpl. C.A. Ryder; Spr. F.J. Manson; Spr. R.H. Johnson; Spr. J.L. Patterson. | Companies: 9th C.I. Bde.; 9th Battn. C.E. | Casualties: none | Movement: D. 4. d. 7.9.–E. 11. c. 0.0.

A. Harris was seriously wounded, who later died of wounds; enemy artillery also sent few gas shells into billets in St. Saulve, causing damage and casualties to the civilian population. | People: Gnr. T. A. Harris. | Casualties: 1 killed (Gnr. T. A. Harris, died of wounds); civilian casualties in St. Saulve (number not given). | Movement: Faubourg de Paris to St. Saulve.

- **1918-11-05 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Wallers** — First 'Flu case from No. 4 Company; extra guards; S.S.O., car driver, runner, Mr Hessey and the Paymaster down with 'Flu; the S.S.O. of 2nd Canadian Division's car broke down and he lunched here. | People: Mr Hessey. | Companies: No. 4 Coy | Casualties: several 'Flu cases | Movement: —

- **1918-11-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Valenciennes, France** — Lieut. R. B. Wallers–Raismes

- **1918-11-06 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Herin** — Dvr. - **1918-11-06 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Onnaing, France** — Shoot carried out in accordance with Operations Order No. 16 from 5.30, 207 rounds fired; at 10.40, 20 rounds fired on targets at S11.c to S.7.a. and S11.a. to S12.c.; roads at M22.c.00.20. and M33a.20.80. continuously harassed 15.00–23.30; during the night road through M.15 and M.21 subjected to harassing fire, 45 rounds fired. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-11-06 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Fenain, France** — No. 48785 Pte. MacDonald E. J. rejoins unit from leave. Admitted 15 horses to M.V.S. | People: No. 48785 Pte. MacDonald E. J. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-11-07 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Valenciennes, France** — One platoon of Canadian Corps cyclists was attached to help build a poled cable route from Valenciennes to Onnaing, 16 O.Rs. proceeded on leave to England and 1 O.R. on leave to France, the Divisional Report Centre was established at Onnaing, No. 4 Section moved from Raismes to Onnaing, and No. 2 Section established a report centre in Quiévrain while 10th C.F.A. moved via Brouta [uncertain] and Corenette [uncertain] to Jemappes. | People: — | Companies: No. 2/3/4 Sections; 10th C.F.A. | Casualties: none | Movement: No. 4 Section Raismes–Onnaing; No. 2 Section to Quiévrain
- **1918-11-07 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Raismes–Onnaing** — Moved via Valenciennes to Onnaing, put up by No. 1 Company; many officers evacuated with 'Flu (Maj. McLeod, Lt. Hessey, Lt. Boyd, Lt. Day, Lt. Gunter); Maj. de Graves and Capt. Danger ill in mild form; Capt. Barlf (Paymaster) evacuated; Lts. George and Glassco sent to run No. 4 Company; wire that Lieut. Rason died of 'Flu, letter written to Lady Rason. | People: Major de Graves, Capt. Danger, Capt. Barlf, Lieut. George, Lieut. Glassco, Major McLeod, Lt. Hessey, Lt. Boyd, Lt. Day, Lt. Gunter, Lieut. [uncertain] shelled, 100 rounds fired; further 71 rounds fired 19.00–21.00 on road at M9.c.2.8 to 5.9 and houses at M8d.7.5 and M8c.9.05. | Casualties: none.

Maxey established a Signal Report Centre in the basement of the Mairie at Quiévrain, work there was then suspended when it was decided to establish Divisional Headquarters at Jemappes instead owing to the deep advance of 7th C.I. Brigade towards Mons, and No. 2 Section could not keep in touch by wire, mounted despatch riders and cyclists being the chief means of communication. | People: Lieut. W. - **1918-11-09 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Onnaing** — Discussed transport with the A.A.Q.M.G.; the chateau owner lunched — the Germans had found his buried wine, confiscated it and fined him 300 francs; Capt. Graham came in as S.S.O.; Capt. Wake and the O.C. sent £205.9.7 each to the Canadian Victory War Loan; Col. MacAlpine sent a subaltern from each other Train to help; Maj. McLeod in hospital. | People: Capt. Graham, Captain Wake, Col. MacAlpine, Major McLeod. | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: —

Onnaing–Jemappes

- **1918-11-10 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Quievrechain** — Pack train arrived 1.30 a.m. and lorries at the dump at 11 a.m.; refilled in the early afternoon; visited H.Q. 5th C.D.A. and reconnoitred near Theulin, 14th Brigade moving to Theulin; Dvr. - **1918-11-11 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Armistice signed at 0500 and fighting ceased at 1100, 1559th day of the War; training in morning; afternoon declared a holiday by General Officer Commanding, all training dispensed with; canteens and messes opened for troops all afternoon; smoker and concert in Sergeants' and Officers' Messes in evening. | Companies: N.S.R.D.
- **1918-11-11 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Mons, Belgium** — Headquarters moved to Mons, the office being established at 1800 hours, a rear office was left in Jemappes to handle No. 3 Section, which had not moved forward, No. 3 Section relieved No. 2 Section in the line after the cessation of hostilities, and 2 pair of D.8 twisted wire were laid between Jemappes and Mons using a further 20,000 yards of cable. | People: — | Companies: No. 2/3 Sections | Casualties: none | Movement: Jemappes–Mons
- **1918-11-11 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Jemappes–Mons** — At 8 a.m. news that the Germans would sign the Armistice at 11 a.m.; Mons captured before daylight; Gen. Sir Arthur Currie made his triumphal entry at 3.30 p.m., addressed the crowd and presented his lance with the Canadian Pennant to the Mayor; Train H.Q. spent the first night after the Armistice in Mons; Lieut. Lawrence reported died in England of the 'Flu. | People: General Sir Arthur Currie, General Stewart, Lieut. Lawrence. | Companies: — | Casualties: Lieut. Lawrence died of influenza (England) | Movement: Train H.Q. Jemappes–Mons
- **1918-11-11 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Thulin, Belgium** — Received order that the D.A. would be in rest. (Armistice.) | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-11-11 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Marchelle, Belgium** — Company moved off at 8 a.m. to Marchelle (M.24 B. Central), the detachment's first entry into Belgium, men and horses fairly comfortably billeted in stables formerly built and occupied by the enemy; the O.C. visited H.Q. 5th C.D.A. in Thulin and read the official wire to cease hostilities at 11 a.m. this date — the Armistice. | People: Dvr. Drewes C., Dvr. Cox P.D., Dvr. Mears G. | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Quievrechain to Marchelle, Belgium
- **1918-11-11 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Onnaing, France** — Message received [one word crossed out — illegible] during the morning: "Hostilities will cease at 11.00 hours on the 11th instant. Troops will stand fast on lines reached at that hour, which will be reported to Corps Headquarters. Censor precautions will be maintained. There will be no intercourse of any description with the enemy. Further instructions will follow. Prowse." | People: Prowse. | Casualties: none.
